companies.name: 2-DTech
companies.description: 2-DTech makes and supplies 2D materials, including CVD-made graphene, graphene platelets, graphene oxide and other 2D materials. The company also offers prototyping of graphene based devices.

companies.name: 2D ApS
companies.description: Denmark-based 2D, a spin-out from the Technical University of Denmark, provides single-layer and multilayered CVD graphene sheets on A4- to meter-sized sacrificial polymer sheets that enables application-agnostic dry transfer without using toxic solvents. The company utilizes a unique large-scale roll-to-roll graphene dry transfer process.

companies.name: 2D Carbon Tech
companies.description: 2D Carbon Tech was established in December 2011 with an aim to develop and produce graphene films. The company is currently offering CVD-produced graphene films on copper, glass, silicon or PET, and also graphene-based touch panels and pressure-sensing films. 2D Carbon Tech's production capacity for graphene films is about 30,000 m 2 /year.

companies.name: 2D Fab AB
companies.description: 2D Fab was established in 2013 as a spin-off from Mid Sweden University in Sweden. The company produces graphene flakes using graphite from the Swedish Woxna Graphite (owned by the Canadian company Flinders Resources ). 2D Fab received venture funding from Miun Venture in 2015.

companies.name: Active-Nano
companies.description: Russia-based Active-nano, established in in 2008, performs research and development in the field of advanced materials, nanomaterials, mechanical activation, mechanochemistry and mechanical alloying.

companies.name: AdNano Technologies
companies.description: AdNano Technologies, based in Karnataka India, produces a range of materials, including several metal oxides. The company has a production line for graphene flakes, with a yearly capacity of 2 tons per year (which can be scaled-up up to 50 tons/per year). The company also produces Graphene Oxide materials with a yearly capacity of up to 100 Kg.

companies.name: Advanced Graphene Products
companies.description: Advanced Graphene Products - AGP is a company that produces and supplies graphene with a primary focus on the engineering and development of graphene based products. AGP produces graphene by a unique method: growth on a liquid metal matrix. The company's HSMG (High Strength Metallurgical Graphene) shows very high mechanical strength and durability, with tests showing up to double the tensile strain resistance compared to CVD. The company transfers graphene onto any desired substrate at customers request. Perfect coverage and continuity makes it the best product for industrial and laboratorial use.

companies.name: Advanced Material Development
companies.description: Advanced Material Development was established in 2017 to commercialize 2D nanomaterial technology from Sussex University in the UK.

companies.name: AirMembrane
companies.description: AirMembrane, established in 2017 in Japan, produces CVD graphene sheets and products based on graphene sheets. The company's main products are transparent graphene conductive films and graphene TEM grids

companies.name: Aninkco
companies.description: Sweden-based Aninkco was established in August 2015 as spin-off from KTH Royal Institute of Technology. The company aims to develop and produce novel conductive inks based on graphene and other 2D materials. In September 2017 Aninkco, together with KTH and Huawei Technologies Sweden received a $120,000 grant from SiO-Grafen - VINNOVA to develop a 3D printing technique to fabricate graphene-coated heat spreaders.

companies.name: Applied Nanolayers / Black Semiconductor Netherlands
companies.description: Applied Nanolayers (ANL), based in the Netherlands, is a 2D material foundry that produces high quality graphene and other 2D materials using a CVD process. The company offers wafers from 50 mm (2-inch) through to 200 mm (8-inch) diameter.

companies.name: Avadain
companies.description: Avadain is a U.S-based producer of graphene flakes. Avadainâs technology produces graphene flakes at low cost using a patented, ecofriendly process. Avadain states that it produces large, thin and very few defect flakes, produced in industrial volumes at a reasonable price.

companies.name: Avanzare
companies.description: Avanzare is a supplier of high-performance nanomaterials for a wide range of applications. The company produces graphene flakes and graphene oxide.

companies.name: AzTrong
companies.description: US-based AzTrong is a producer of functionalized graphene ( GO and rGO) materials in the forms of inks, powders, slurries and films. AzTrong has a 100-ton production facility in Taiwan. In addition to its graphene supply business, AzTrong developed dispersion and thin-film coating deposition methods to achieve graphene functionalization and composites.

companies.name: Be Dimensional
companies.description: Be Dimensional is an Italian early-stage startup, spun off from the IIT scientific research centre. It is dedicated to the development of new materials for the manufacturing industry by introducing 2-dimensional new crystalline crystals, including graphene. Be Dimensional also provides development and consultation services.

companies.name: BeeGraphene
companies.description: BeeGraphene, established in Poland in 2020, produces high-quality graphene sheets grown on silicon carbide. The company also offers graphene c haracterization and instrumentation services.

companies.name: BESTGRAPHENE
companies.description: BESTGRAPHENE is a South-Korean company with specialized graphene technology that supplies graphene application materials to various industrial fields, through synthesis of graphene raw materials, functionalization, and production of intermediate materials using them.

companies.name: Bio Graphene Solutions (BGS)
companies.description: Bio Graphene Solutions (BGS) is a Canada-based manufacturer and supplier of graphene from non-graphite based, organic renewable resources.

companies.name: Black Swan Graphene
companies.description: Black Swan Graphene was established in July 2021, by Mason Graphite and Thomas Swan . BSG owns patented graphene processing technologies developed at Thomas Swan. In 2022, Black Swan Graphene went public in the TSX stock exchange (SWAN.V).

companies.name: BLACKLEAF
companies.description: BLACKLEAF is a France-based company that aims to make graphene affordable and enable the industry to reshape products with a greener and more efficient approach. The company produces Few Layer Graphene (FLG) based on a proprietary method. BLACKLEAF says its process results in high quality materials that is dispersed in a 98% water-based solution.

companies.name: Boomatech
companies.description: Brazil-based Boomatech produces graphene, graphene oxide and r-GO materials. The company developed its own production (a mix of Hummers + Tours + proprietary knowledge). The company's GO production capacity is around 100 Kg per month. Boomatech also develops graphene-based applications, currently focused on graphene batteries.

companies.name: Bright Day Graphene
companies.description: Founded in Sweden in 2017, Bright Day Graphene (BDG) strives to offer high performing materials without harmful environmental impacts.

companies.name: Carbon Gates Technology
companies.description: Carbon Gates Technologies (CGT) is an early-stage company that was spun-out of Texas A&M University in 2018. CGT produces high quality graphene flakes (GNPs). The company says that its proprietary graphite exfoliation production process results in large graphene nanoplatelets, with very low D/G peak.

companies.name: Carbon Nano-Material Technology
companies.description: Carbon Nano-Material Technology is a South Korean refined graphite and graphene carbon materials manufacturer. It holds several patents and further patents pending relating to processes for the manufacture of these materials at significantly lower costs than other manufacturers. The company is already said to be selling value added graphite products in the market using its proprietary portfolio of technologies. Carbon Nano-Material Technology has developed mass-production technology at a cost of 20 to 30% of existing technology in-house for the first time in the world by enhancing catalyst production and synthesis in the existing production process of carbon nano-material

companies.name: Carbon Research and Development Company (CRDC)
companies.description: US-based Carbon Research and Development Company (CRDC) produces graphene materials, derived from bio-mass. CRDC's materials are branded as Xphene.

companies.name: Carbon Waters
companies.description: France-based Carbon Waters produces graphene materials using a unique patented process that produce high-quality graphene in water dispersion.

companies.name: Carbonext
companies.description: Carbonext is based in Oklahoma, specializing in commercial graphene technology applications.

companies.name: CealTech
companies.description: CealTech, established in 2012, is a graphene producer that patented a 3D graphene production method. The company aims to produce graphene at an industrial scale, and enable the development and commercialization of graphene-based products.

companies.name: Ceylon Graphene Technologies
companies.description: Sri Lanka based Ceylon Graphene Technologies was established in June 2018 as a joint venture of the LOLC Group and the Sri Lanka Institute of Nanotechnology (SLINTEC). CGT produces high-quality graphene and other carbon materials using Sri Lanka graphite.

companies.name: CHARMGRAPHENE
companies.description: Charmgraphene, based in Korea, is producing graphene materials - both CVD graphene (using a roll-to-roll facility) and graphene flakes. The company's R2R production system can produce 2 meters of CVD graphene per minute (maximum width 300 mm). The company also offers custom-built materials production equipment, such as ALD, Evaporators, and more.

companies.name: Chongqing Graphene Technology
companies.description: Chongqing Graphene Technology (also known, apparently, as Chongqing Moxi Technology) was established in March 2013 as a joint-venture between the Shanghai Nanjiang Group and the Chongqing Institute of Green Intelligent Technology. Chongqing Graphene Technology produces CVD graphene sheets and the company also offers touch panels and other films that use graphene sheets. The company says its production line can produce up to 3 million sheets per year (but we do not know the size of each sheet).

companies.name: CUMI Grafino
companies.description: Grafino is a range of graphene products from Carborundum Universal Ltd (CUMI), a maker of engineering materials that is a part of Chennai based Murugappa Group. CUMI Grafino has a yearly capacity to produce 4MT of Graphene powders and 20 MT of Graphene polymer composites.

companies.name: CVD Materials Corporation
companies.description: CVD Materials Corporation is a subsidiary of CVD Equipment that manufactures and supplies advanced materials, metal surface treatments, and coatings.

companies.name: CVMR Corporation
companies.description: CVMR Corporation is a privately held multinational organization with its head office and R&D Center in Toronto, Canada.

companies.name: Danish Graphene
companies.description: Danish Graphene produces and supplies graphene materials for industrial composites to enhance performance and lifetime of products. Danish Graphene relies on research from the Department of Chemistry at Aarhus University.

companies.name: Deyang Carbonene
companies.description: Deyang Graphene Science and Technology (also known as Deyang Carbonen) is a graphene producer with an annual capacity of 1.5 tons. Deyang Carbonen plans to expand their facilities to 300 yearly tons).Â The company also develops graphene applications, such as anti-corrosion coating and heat conducting materials.

companies.name: Directa Plus
companies.description: Directa Plus was established in 2005 in Italy to develop innovative nanomaterial production processes. The company developed its own exfoliation process (which they call G+) that can be used to produce super-expanded graphite, pristine GNPs, water-dispersed GNPs and fine nanographite powder (all of them marketed under the G+ brand).

companies.name: Enerage
companies.description: Enerage, based in Taiwan, was established in 2005 to develop fuel cell technologies. In 2010 the company shifted its focus to graphene technologies, and has developed its own production process based on high pressure liquid exfoliation.

companies.name: Fanglin Minerals
companies.description: China-based Fanglin Minerals was established in 1993 to produce and supply magnesite and silicon carbide products and minerals. The company is also producing reduced graphene oxide (r-GO). The company's capacity is about 200 ton per year.

companies.name: Faradyne Power
companies.description: Faradyne Power was formed in 2023 by veteran executives, scientists and entrepreneurs from the graphene, power utility, and energy innovation sectors. Their combined skill sets and business knowledge enabled Faradyne to quickly scale up and start commercializing its unique 'turbostratic' graphene.

companies.name: Fuxi Technology
companies.description: China-based Fuxi Technology develops thermal solutions based on the graphene technologies. The company's products include graphene thermal films for the consumer electronics, aerospace, medical and other industries.

companies.name: Garmor
companies.description: Garmor Inc, based in Orlando, Florida, was spun-off the University of Central Florida to develop a new cost-effective and environmentally-friendly graphene oxide flakes production process. Garmor aims to manufacture and sell graphene. In July 2021, Asbury Carbons acquired Garmor.

companies.name: General Graphene Corporation
companies.description: General Graphene Corp (GGC) is a CVD graphene producer, that uses its own manufacturing technology to provide graphene sheets in industrial quantities at marketable prices. GGC technology originates from production methods licensed from the University of Texas (UT) and Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). According to the company, its annual capacity is up to 100,000 sqm.

companies.name: Golden Formula
companies.description: Russia-based Golden Formula is a producer of a unique nano-absorbent high reactivity carbon mixture (HRCM). The company develops and produces filters and water purification systems based on the HRCM mixture. HRCM is mostly composed of graphene-materials, produced by Golden Formula themselves.

companies.name: GoLeafe
companies.description: US-based GOLeafe is a graphene development company that produces spherical graphene oxide, reduced graphene, boron doped graphene, phosphorus doped graphene as well nitrogen doped graphene. GoLeafe's graphene is produced at the company's overseas plant and handled in GoLeafe's Durham site. The materials are characterized, packaged and exclusively sold by Kyma Technologies.

companies.name: Grafoid
companies.description: Grafoid is a private company based in Canada that aims to produce graphene on a commercial scale using their proprietary extraction process. The company is also active in high-growth, scalable graphene projects, patents and material applications.

companies.name: Graphenano
companies.description: Graphenano, based in Alicante, Spain and established in 2011 is a graphene and carbon nanofiber producer that is collaborating with the University of Castilla La Mancha in Ciudad Real.

companies.name: Graphene & Solar Technologies (GSTX)
companies.description: Graphene & Solar Technologies is a developer of Renewable Alternative Energy systems. It has interests in High Purity Quartz mineral deposits, Photovoltaics (PV), and essential materials production, as well as essential production materials for the high-end electronics and semi-conductor production materials.

companies.name: Graphene Laboratories
companies.description: Graphene Laboratories Inc. located in Ronkonkoma, NY, is a subsidiary of G6 Materials (TSXV: GGG $GGG.V $GPHBF ). The Company manufactures a variety of graphene-related products including Graphene Oxide and Chemical Vapor Deposition Graphene.

companies.name: Graphene Layers
companies.description: Graphene Layers is a start-up company located in New Jersey developing a manufacturing technology of graphene-based solutions, focused on developing and commercializing advanced materials and technologies that have the potential to revolutionize various industries including OSW sector.

companies.name: Graphene Leaders Canada
companies.description: Graphene Leaders Canada (GLC) is a Canada-based graphene supplier and applications developer (focused on the energy sector and water filtration). The company developed its own graphite-exfoliation method to produce graphene and uses Canadian mined graphite to produce GO and rGO materials.

companies.name: Graphene Manufacturing Group (GMG)
companies.description: Australia-based Graphene Manufacturing Group (GMG) was founded in 2016 to create a business to manufacture bulk graphene materials. GMG uses a proprietary production process and the company focuses on solutions for the energy storage and energy saving markets.

companies.name: Graphene Nano
companies.description: Graphene Nano LLC Joint Venture is an Uzbekistan-based company that produces advanced graphene-based materials. Its main products include: - Graphene Aerogels - Graphene Oxide Dispersions - Graphene Oxide Powders

companies.name: Graphene Production
companies.description: Founded in 2015, Graphene Production is a European producer of graphene, with a 90 tons/year production capacity (as per the Company's website). Graphene Production is also an engineering company with its fully equipped laboratory.

companies.name: Graphene Star
companies.description: Graphene Star Ltd is a UK manufacturing company producing high quality graphene and graphitic materials.

companies.name: Graphene Waves
companies.description: Graphene Waves develops large area and homogenous epitaxial graphene with high uniformity. The Company is involved in graphene manufacture and characterization, and production of quantum Hall effect devices.

companies.name: Graphene-XT
companies.description: Graphene-XT (previously GNext) is a startup that develops and produces high quality graphene. It actively collaborates with customers with the aim of improving product characteristics and designing personalized solutions. Through a multi-functional approach it provides new and better functionalities to conventional products.

companies.name: Graphenea
companies.description: Graphenea, a technology company founded in 2010, is a leading graphene producer. Graphenea focuses on contributing to the successful development of Graphene applications of its customers, in a wide range of sectors and in more than 60 countries in the world. Through research and innovation, it supports its customers with a portfolio consisting of: CVD Graphene films, Graphene Field-Effect-Transistors chips (GFETs), Graphene Foundry Services (GFAB) and Graphene Oxides. Graphenea’s facilities are located in Spain (San Sebastián) and USA (Boston).

companies.name: Graphenel JSC
companies.description: Graphenel JSC, founded in 2011, is a technology company focusing on mass graphene manufacturing and its applications. It unique approachis to refine animal fat to produce cost-effective mass production of graphene.

companies.name: Graphenelab limited
companies.description: GrapheneLab Limited is a privately-held UK-based graphene producer established in 2015. The company produces chemically-pure low-cost GNPs, based on low-temperature physical exfoliation of natural or artificial graphite in deionized water. The company is also developing applications for thermal interface material, Li-Ion batteries and composite materials.

companies.name: Graphenemex
companies.description: Graphenemex was established in 2016 in Mexico with an aim to become a high quality graphene producer and applications developer. The company currently produces both graphene flakes, graphene oxide, reduced graphene oxide and CVD graphene. Graphenemex's current capacity for graphene flakes and GO is about one ton per year.

companies.name: Graphenest
companies.description: Portugal-based Graphenest developed a novel method for large production of high quality graphene nanoplatelets and their functional derivatives from natural graphite. Grahpenest is currently producing and selling graphene flakes (GNPS) of various qualities.

companies.name: Graphensic
companies.description: Graphensic was established in November 2011 in Sweden as a spin-off from Linköping University and became the first European supplier of epitaxial graphene on silicon carbide.

companies.name: Grapherry
companies.description: Grapherry specializes in the scalable and low-cost production of graphene and its applications. It produces high-quality graphene through a proprietary, scalable, continuous-flow process and then customizes the material for specific applications in soil, construction, and energy systems, ensuring consistent performance and cost efficiency.

companies.name: Graphite Innovation & Technologies
companies.description: Established in 2016 in Canada, Graphite Innovation & Technologies (GIT) is an R&D Company that develops and produces high quality graphene flakes (GNPs). GIT also develops advanced engineered materials customized for specific applications and technologies.

companies.name: Graphitene
companies.description: Graphitene, established in 2013 in the UK, produces graphite compounds, graphene and graphene oxide in lab-scale in collaboration with NTNU in Norway and Cambridge University in the UK. In 2015 the company's small-scale manufacturing plant in the UK commenced production. The company is also engaged in various graphite and graphene R&D projects.

companies.name: Graphjet Technology
companies.description: Established in 2019 in Malaysia, Graphjet Technology supplies sustainable low-cost graphene, graphite and graphene-based anode materials.

companies.name: Grolltex
companies.description: Grolltex (short for "graphene-rolling-technologies") is an advanced materials and equipment company located in San Diego, California. The company produces high-quality and low-cost CVD graphene using a unique roll-to-roll process, developed at the University of California, San Diego.

companies.name: GTechPlasma
companies.description: GTechPlasma is a Portuguese deep-tech spin-off from Instituto Superior Técnico’s Institute for Plasmas and Nuclear Fusion, focused on producing high-quality graphene and graphene derivatives using plasma technology. It a startup built around patented technology, with applications in electromagnetic shielding, stealth/radar-absorbing coatings, rare-earth and uranium extraction, and solid-state hydrogen storage.

companies.name: Haydale
companies.description: Haydale Graphene Industries produces and supplies graphene GNPs and graphene-based products. Haydale developed a patented proprietary scalable plasma process to functionalize graphene and other nanomaterials. The company does not produce the basic graphene material, but functionzalizes it. Haydale is a public company that trades at the AIM (AIM:HAYD).

companies.name: Hazer Group
companies.description: Hazer Group is an early stage technology development company undertaking the commercialization of the Hazer Process, a low-emission hydrogen and graphite production process. The Hazer Process was developed by researchers at The University of Western Australia (UWA), before the IP were assigned to Hazer for further commercial development.

companies.name: Hexorp
companies.description: India-based Hexorp produces graphene materials for industrial markets that uses its own propreitary method that results in high-purity materials. Hexorp currently offers few-layer graphene flakes powder, and is also developing other materials including Graphene Oxide and graphene composites.

companies.name: Highbery New Nano Materials Technology
companies.description: Established in 2016, China-based Highbery Nano New Material Technology developed graphene-enhanced polymers, with a focus on graphene-nylon fibers. It seems as if Highbery is no longer in business.

companies.name: hq graphene
companies.description: HQ Graphene is a nanotechnology company, specialized in the production and characterization of two-dimensional crystals like hexagonal boron nitride, high quality single crystal graphene, single large size crystals of sulphides, tellurides and more.

companies.name: HydroGraph Clean Power
companies.description: HydroGraph Clean Power, established in 2017 in the US, commercializes a unique graphene production technology that was developed at Kansas State University. The process is based on detonation of hydrocarbons that is said to produce extremely high purity graphene.

companies.name: Hygraner
companies.description: Hygraner is an Italy-based startup that was established in 2016 with an aim to produce graphene-based materials. The company main products are based on recycled PET fibers and polypropylene fibers, both enhanced with graphene. The company also offer fabrics made from its fiber materials and other graphene-based materials.

companies.name: Incubation Alliance
companies.description: Incubation Alliance was established in 2007 in Kobe, Japan to manufacture and sale carbon materials. The company is offering so-called Graphene Flower materials: substrate-free and catalyst-free multi layer graphene material made by direct synthesis.

companies.name: Jälle Technologies
companies.description: Jälle Technologies is an Estonian deeptech company developing recycling processes to recover critical materials from used lithium-ion batteries.

companies.name: JMC
companies.description: JMC (originally the Jeil Moolsan Company), owned by the KISCO group, produces fine chemical products, such as reactive dyes, medicinal intermediates, electronics, plastics, and agriculture. JMC is also a large-scale producer of the artificial sweetener Saccharin.

companies.name: KB Element
companies.description: KB Element started with the technology needed to control static electricity and particles which are catastrophic in semiconductor and display processes. Based on this technology, the Company says it succeeded in the mass production of ‘Non-oxidized Graphene’.

companies.name: KennedyLabs
companies.description: KennedyLabs, based in Canada and spun off from the National Research Council in Canada, is a boutique material maker that produces graphene sheets (CVD), graphene oxide and graphene inks. The company is also producing other 2D materials (i.e. hBN) and it

companies.name: Knano
companies.description: Knano (the full name is Xiamen Knano Graphene Technology Co) specializes in graphene R&D, production and sales. Knano holds more than 40 patents and develops graphene for several applications - including energy storage, composites, coatings and more. Knano's graphene flake production capacity is a few dozens of tons per year, and i t is building a 250 tons per year (graphene and graphene-based materials) facility .

companies.name: KNV'S Incorporation
companies.description: KNV's was established in 2010 by the Sharma family, to manufacture construction and flame retardant chemicals. The company expanded into graphene production in 2015. KNV currently produces 1-3 layer graphene flakes in bulk for both research and industrial applications. The company sells graphene and graphene oxide, as well as graphene-enhanced inks.

companies.name: KoreaGraph
companies.description: KoreaGraph was founded in 2012 in Seoul, Korea, with the aim to become a CVD graphene producer. The company developed its own refined manufacturing process which is said to be highly cost-effective.

companies.name: LayerOne
companies.description: LayerOne (previously called Abalonyx), is engaged in the production of graphene oxide and derivatives of graphene oxide, as well as related R&D.

companies.name: LeaderNano (Jiling)
companies.description: LeaderNano, based in Jiling, China, develops and produces advanced nanomaterias - including graphene, graphene oxide, nitrogen and boron doped graphene, GNPs and other materials (such as MoS 2 and WS 2 ).

companies.name: Matrexia Advanced Technologies
companies.description: Matrexia Advanced Technologies was founded in March 2025 after nearly five years of intensive research and development and is focused on manufacturing graphene via its proprietary manufacturing process. It is a fully bootstrapped organization which is part of India’s Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) and startup initiatives.

companies.name: MCK Tech
companies.description: Korea based MCK, established in 2017, produces CVD graphene materials and develops applications based on these materials. MCK uses its proprietary rapid-thermal CVD (RT-CVD) process, currently in batch mode operation (with roll-to-roll process under development, in collaboration with the Korean Institute of Machinery and Materials).

companies.name: Morgan Advanced Materials
companies.description: Morgan Advanced Materials , based in the UK and founded in 1856, is an advanced materials technology company with a global presence. The company is active in many markets, including medical instruments, aerospace, power generation and trains. It is also active with carbon processing for over 150 years. In August 2014, Morgan Advanced Materials signed a joint-development agreement with the University of Manchester to scale-up a new graphene manufacturing process.

companies.name: Morion NanoTech / Mo Rui Technology
companies.description: Morion NanoTech (or: Mo Rui Technology) is a materials company founded in Dongguan, China, that specializes in the application and development of graphene and other micro-nano materials.

companies.name: Nanesa
companies.description: Nanesa is an Italian-based start-up company that aims to produce and market conductive silver-based inks, pastes and graphene based materials. The company currently offers graphene flakes, graphene oxide and graphene-based thermal foils.

companies.name: Nano Carbon (Poland)
companies.description: Nano Carbon was established in 2011 in Poland to engage in graphene research and production. The company uses technology developed at the Institute of Electronic Materials Technology in Warsaw and is co-owned by mining giant KGHM and the Polish Armaments Group (PGZ)

companies.name: Nanoacts
companies.description: Nanoacts Ltd. is a deep-tech company developing patented HHO (Brown’s gas) plasma technologies that convert carbon waste (plastics, tires, biomass, biochar, CO₂, carbon black) into high-quality graphene, graphene oxide (GO), reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and hybrid nanomaterials in a single, clean step.

companies.name: NanoEMI
companies.description: Poland-based NanoEMI is producing graphene flakes using two different methods (exfoliation in isopropyl alcohol and in castor oil). The company's has a pilot production line. NanoEMI is focused on EMI shielding applications. The company also offers material engineering services.

companies.name: NanoGrafen
companies.description: NanoGrafen was established in 2013 in Turkey as an nanotechnology R&D and consulting company. The company produces high-quality graphene and develops graphene-based applications. NanoGrafen also provides technical consultancy about the development of graphene based composites, the preparation of masterbatches and formulation developments.

companies.name: Nanografi
companies.description: Nanografi is a Turkia-based company established in 2011 to develop and produce nanomaterials, including carbon based materials such as graphene and CNTs. Nanografi currently offers several kinds of graphene flakes (GNPs), and silicon-graphene nano composites.

companies.name: NanoIntegris
companies.description: NanoIntegris (a subsidiary of Raymor Industries) produces, purifies and processes several grades of conductive carbon, carbon nanotubes and few-layer graphene flakes. The company uses different exfoliation methods to produce the graphene flakes. Nanointegris service the industrial and academic R&D market with over 600 clients worldwide.

companies.name: Nanomatrix Materials
companies.description: India-based Nanomatrix Materials (NM Materials) produces graphene oxide materials and also develops applications based on graphene. The company offers raw graphene materials (GO and r-GO) and also products such as oil absorbants, air filters and face masks .

companies.name: NanoTechCenter
companies.description: Russia-based NanoTechCenter is a graphene flake (GNP) and CNT producer that uses technology developed at Tambov's State Technical University (TSTU). NanoTechCenter's material are used in the energy, composite and water treatment markets, and the company also develops and manufactures composites production equipment.

companies.name: NanoXplore
companies.description: NanoXplore is a graphene company, a manufacturer and supplier of high-volume graphene powder for use in industrial markets, mostly as a replacement for carbon black, but also for other use cases.

companies.name: Nanum
companies.description: Nanum Nanotechnology is a Brazilian company in the Fine Chemicals sector, recognized for the development and commercialization of innovative solutions based on nanotechnology. Its portfolio includes metallic nanoparticles, nano-structured metal oxides, and carbon nanostructures, specializing in nanoparticle dispersion and functionalization.

companies.name: NeoGraf Solutions
companies.description: US-based NeoGraf Solutions is a producer of high-performance carbon and graphite products for over 140 years, for a variety of demanding applications and industries. In 2021, NeoGraf started producing graphene materials, including GNPs and graphene precursors in a new production facility, with a yearly capacity of 750 tons (GNPs) and 1,300 tons (graphene precursors). NeoGraf uses multiple top-down exfoliation methods starting with natural graphite.

companies.name: Nippon Shokubai
companies.description: Nippon Shokubai is a Japan-based, global chemical company.

companies.name: Nordische Technologies
companies.description: Nordische Technologies Pvt Ltd, based in India, and with operations in Germany and the UK, was established in 2019 to develop graphene technologies and applications. Nodische produces graphene using chemical exfoliation, and has a capacity of around 1Kg per day. The company focuses on electronic vehicle charging and other related technologies

companies.name: Nova Graphene
companies.description: Canada-based Nova Graphene is a graphene producer that makes graphene flakes in several grades, under the CarbonEra brand. The company says it has a production capacity of over 1,000 tons per year. Areas of focus include concrete & asphalt, additive manufacturing, expansion foams, and ballistic materials.

companies.name: Novusterra
companies.description: Novusterra Inc. is a specialty chemical company that produces graphene from carbon based deposits.

companies.name: NTherma Corporation
companies.description: US-based NTherma produces multi-walled carbon nanotubes and graphene. NTherma produces graphene flakes (GNPs), graphene ribbons and also graphene-based oil additives.

companies.name: Perpetuus Advanced Materials
companies.description: Perpetuus Advanced Materials (once known as Perpetuus Carbon) focuses on manufacturing plasma-treated, surface engineered graphenes and sub-micron particles for commercial uses. The company is based in the UK and seems to be active again, after years in which it seemed to be closed.

companies.name: Phi4Tech
companies.description: Spain-based Phi4Tech is a group of nanotechnology companies, active in several fields, including energy storage, nanomaterial production, and medical and industrial polymers.

companies.name: Plasmaphene
companies.description: Plasmaphene is a Portuguese industrial deep-tech company focused on graphene and related two-dimensional nanomaterials. Based in Vila Viçosa, the company uses proprietary plasma-based processes to produce high-quality graphene, graphene nanoplatelets, and nitrogen-doped graphene with an emphasis on consistency, purity, and scalability.

companies.name: Plastic 2 Green
companies.description: Technology startup Plastic 2 Green aims to unlock the energy potential of waste plastic via novel technologies to convert plastic waste to ammonia - the most efficient method for storing hydrogen energy - and high demand specialty carbon products like graphene and CNTs.

companies.name: PranaGraf
companies.description: PranaGraf (previously called Tirupati Specialty Graphite) is a producer of various advanced materials like expandable graphite, high purity natural graphite, anode materials and graphene. PranaGraf has been manufacturing graphene using its proprietary zero-chemical process since 2019, using in-house manufactured high purity graphite as input.

companies.name: Quantum Max
companies.description: Quantum Max is a startup located in TamilNadu, India. It produces graphene as an additive product for architectural paints, graphene lubricants for engine oil and heat dissipation coatings. The Company manufacture functionalized graphene using its proprietary method of production. The functionalization disperses graphene in water, polar and non polar solvents, PU, epoxies and more without any need of external additives and keeps it stable without agglomeration. It blends with PET, LDPE and other hot melt extruded plastics without any extra processes or chemicals.

companies.name: Rasco-Energo
companies.description: Rasco-Energo, headquartered in the Germany, is an international trading and development company that specializes in the procurement of spare parts, metal alloys, and the processing of metallic materials. In 2026, Rasco-Energo entered the graphene industry, and has setup a 9 ton per month GNP production facility in the UAE. The process is based on a proprietary ultrasonic technology. The company offers a range of graphene flakes, including 2D and 2.5D graphene (99% carbon) in aqueous suspension form, bilayer graphene, multilayer graphene (5+ layers), and activated graphene.

companies.name: Rimere
companies.description: Rimere is an advanced plasma technology company, inspired by naturally occurring phenomena, focused on providing cost-effective and practical climate solutions, zero emissions hydrogen, and valuable nano-carbon materials. Rimere’s sequential hybrid plasma technology allows breaking apart methane molecules and reconfiguring them into cleaner alternatives. Its Reformer device produces multiple grades of nanocarbon products including high purity graphene.

companies.name: Saiyin Materials
companies.description: Saiyin Materials is a China-based company that specializes in the large-scale production and supply of graphene powders, produced from carbon black using a Rapid Joule Heating (RJH) process. The company's production capacity is reportedly scalable to 600 tons per year, with a focus on cost-effective graphene materials for industrial applications. Its graphene materials are mainly used in:

companies.name: Sea Further
companies.description: Sea Further is a Monaco-based startup founded in 2020, specializing in nanotechnology research for sustainable industrial processes, particularly biologically-based doped graphene production. The company develops innovative processes for clean industry using new carbon materials like graphene oxide doping via microbial activities, holding a key patent in this area. It aims to balance environmental respect with profitability, led by founder and CEO Iakimov Valentino.

companies.name: Shanghai SIMBATT Energy Technology
companies.description: Shanghai-based SIMBATT Energy Technology is developing, producing and marketing graphene powder materials. SIMBATT currently offers intercalated graphite, graphene oxide, graphene powder, doped graphene powder, graphene quantum dot and other materials.

companies.name: Sixonia Tech
companies.description: Germany-based Sixonia Tech was established in 2017 as a spin-out from the Technical University of Dresden. The company produces and markets a range of functionalized and pristine large-flake, few-layer electrochemically exfoliated graphene ("E-Graphenes") materials and formulations. Sixonia Tech currently offers tailor-made E-Graphene materials, customized formulations and R&D projects to companies and research institutes in the packaging, electronics, wearables and aerospace sectors based on its own IP.

companies.name: Source Graphene
companies.description: Source Graphene, based in Romania and established in 2017, is a graphene oxide producer and supplier. Source Graphene is producing its GO materials from raw graphite using proprietary separation and washing methods.

companies.name: Spnano
companies.description: Israel-based Spnano was established in 2007 was a spin-off from the Hebrew University. Spnano's technology is based on an innovative protein (SP1) which enables the production of superior composite materials, based on either Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs) or graphene materials.

companies.name: Standard Graphene
companies.description: Standard Graphene is a Korea-based company with large production capabilities, offering graphene and graphene oxide materials and also intermediate graphene-based materials such as graphene-polyurethane solutions, graphene-polymer compounds, graphene-carbon-fiber prepreg and various coating solutions.

companies.name: SurgePower Materials
companies.description: US-based SurgePower Materials produces monolayer graphene using a patented green and sustainable production process. The company offers three grades of graphene with varying surface areas and carbon content. SurgePower is scaling up its production process to achieve a yearly capacity of around 36 tons.

companies.name: Syrah Resources
companies.description: Syrah Resources is an Australian industrial minerals and technology company producing graphite, graphene and battery anode materials (AAM). In August 2025, Syrah Resources raised AUD$42 million (around USD$27 million).

companies.name: Talga Resources
companies.description: Talga Resources Ltd is a multi-national company focused on graphite mining and graphene supply and application development. The company mines graphite in Sweden, operates a test processing facility in Germany under Talga Advanced Materials GmbH and has a product development arm, Talga Technologies UK Ltd located in Cambridge, UK.

companies.name: Tata Steel
companies.description: Tata group is a multinational enterprise, headquartered in India, that includes over 100 independent operating companies. Tata Steel is considered as Tata Group's flagship company and is one of the leading steel producers in the world. Tata Steel has been active in the field of graphene R&D for many years, with work that ranges from steel-related projects back in 2014 , through releasing a graphene-based product range - the Tiscon Superlinks+ graphene-coated stirrups in 2017, to ongoing development and commercialization work.

companies.name: Tenutec
companies.description: Tenutec provides graphene materials and products used in various areas, currently primarily in thermal management. It has a unique single-step production method that is able to provide eco-friendly, high-quality graphene customized to customers' needs.

companies.name: Textile Two Dimensional
companies.description: UK-based Textile Two Dimensional was spun-off from the University of Cambridge with support from the Royal Academy of Engineering, to develop graphene and other 2D material based inks for textile applications. Textile Two Dimensional offers graphene-based inks and printing and integration services.

companies.name: The Advanced Carbons Company (TACC)
companies.description: TACC, a wholly owned subsidiary of HEG, is an India-based company specializing in advanced carbon and synthetic graphite technologies. TACC is driving innovation across both synthetic graphite-based Anode Active Material (AAM) and graphene derivatives, two critical components in the global energy storage and industrial ecosystems.

companies.name: The Sixth Element Materials
companies.description: The Sixth Element Materials Technology company, based in Chengzhou, China, is developing and producing graphene flakes, graphene oxide and related materials. The company also holds 30% of Wuxi Graphene Film , a CVD-graphene film maker based in Wuxi, China. The company says their current graphene-powder production capacity is 100 tons per year, and they plan to increase it to 1,000 tons by the end of 2016. In July 2016 we interviewed the company's new Europrean sales manager on the company's technology and business. In October 2017 the company updated that its graphene-enhanced anti-corrosion coating has been deployed in bridges and other structures across China .

companies.name: Thomas Swan
companies.description: Thomas Swan is a privately held global chemical manufacturing company. The company produces a broad range of additives, resins and active pharmaceutical ingredients, custom manufacture work and advanced materials. The company claims to be the world leader in the manufacture of single-wall carbon nanotubes. In March 2014 Thomas Swan launched graphene powder and water/surfactant dispersed graphene nanoplatelet s .

companies.name: TMTP Labs
companies.description: Nanotechnology startup TMTP Labs (New Orleans, La., U.S.) specializes in graphene and advanced materials research.

companies.name: Tokyo Chemical Industry
companies.description: Tokyo Chemical Industry (TCI) is a global manufacturer and distributor of specialty organic chemicals with facilities in the USA, Europe, Japan, China and India. TCI offers several nano-carbon materials, including CNTs, fullerenes, nanodiamonds, graphene materials (GNPs) and graphene oxide materials. See more here .

companies.name: Toray Industries
companies.description: Toray Industries is a Japanese corporation, active since 1926, which develops, manufactures and and sells various products in such fields as: fibers & textiles, performance chemicals, carbon-based composites, environment, life sciences and much more. To date, Toray has developed technologies to create top-quality graphene from inexpensive graphite materials. One of its recent graphene materials is an ultra-thin graphene dispersion solution with excellent fluidity and electrical and thermal conductivity.

companies.name: Turquoise Group
companies.description: Turquoise Group is an Australian clean energy company headquartered in Brisbane, commercializing a plasma-based process to make low-cost graphene and hydrogen out of methane gas. Turquoise Group aims to mass produce low-cost, high-quality graphene to unlock its true potential as a substitute feedstock for a wide range of next-generation products.

companies.name: Universal Matter
companies.description: Universal Matter has developed "cleaner, faster, and less expensive" technology to commercialize graphene. The company's tech is based on the Rice University lab of chemist James Tour's proprietary Flash Joule Heating process that can convert inexpensive carbon sources into graphene layers. Headquartered in Burlington, Ontario, Canada, with U.S. headquarters in Houston, Universal Matter’s vision is to build on its strong R&D foundation to scale its production process and become the world’s leading supplier of lower cost and higher quality graphene materials from petcoke, agricultural feedstocks, recycled plastic, recycled rubber and coal.

companies.name: Universal Matter GBR (formerly: Applied Graphene Materials)
companies.description: Universal Matter GBR (formerly: Applied Graphene Materials, previously Durham Graphene Science) was established in 2010 as a spin-off from Durham University to develop a new graphene synthesis method and produce graphene materials. AGM's technology was a unique patented scalable 'bottom-up' CVD approach to produce graphene.

companies.name: Urbix Resources
companies.description: Urbix Resources was founded in 2014 with the goal of creating radical change in the way natural graphite is refined and commercialized. Urbix specializes in all aspects of the graphite value chain, and is a premier provider of Graphite Ore, Refined Graphite Powders, Graphene, and other advanced Graphite Products.

companies.name: Versarien
companies.description: Founded in 2010, Versarien (AIM:VRS) is an advanced materials group leveraging proprietary technology to create innovative engineering solutions for its clients in a diverse range of industries.

companies.name: VNGraphene
companies.description: VN Graphene (officially Applied Nanotechnology or ANTECH) was established in 2010 in Vietnam with an aim to become a nanotechnology material producer. In 2016 VNGraphene started to produce graphene flakes (GNPs) using direct chemical exfoliation, a plant that had a production capacity of 1Kg/day, with plans to upgrade that to 5-10 kg/day.

companies.name: Volt Carbon Technologies
companies.description: Volt Carbon Technologies (previously known as Saint Jean Carbon) is a publicly traded junior mining exploration company with graphite mining claims on five 100% Company-owned properties located in the province of Quebec in Canada. The five properties include the Walker property, a past producing mine, the Wallingford property, the St. Jovite property, East Miller and Clot Property. The Company also holds the Page graphite property in Ontario.

companies.name: Vorbeck Materials
companies.description: Vorbeck Materials is a U.S-based company that manufactures its own graphene materials (Vor-x®), conductive inks (Vor-ink™), and high-performance electronic components for advanced applications.

companies.name: William Blythe
companies.description: William Blythe, a wholly owned subsidiary of Synthomer PLC, is a manufacturer of inorganic speciality chemicals and advanced materials. WB's portfolio currently covers Iodine, Tin, Copper and Tungsten derivatives as well as advanced materials, among others Graphene Oxide. Application areas that William Blythe focuses on are Catalysts, Coatings, Electronics, Life Sciences, Pigment, Polymer Additives, and many others.

companies.name: XFNano
companies.description: China-based Nanjing XFNANO Materials Tech (XFNano), founded in 2009, mainly focuses on the R&D and manufacture of graphene, graphene oxide, and graphene-like materials such as graphene quantum dots, carbon nanotubes, MoS 2 , WS 2, silver nanowires and molecular sieves.

companies.name: 2D Generation
companies.description: 2D Generation is an Israel-based company that has developed a solution to enable in-situ ALD graphene deposition at low temperatures. At the end of 2024, 2D Generation was acquired by Adysin .

companies.name: 2D Photonics
companies.description: 2D Photonics develops ultra-high bandwidth, low latency optical interconnect transceivers used to reduce the infrastructure cost and energy consumption of generative AI, cellular, and strategic data transfer systems. The Company's Graphene Integrated Photonics (GIP) offers superior capabilities for next-generation transceivers.

companies.name: 3D Graphtech Industries
companies.description: 3D Graphtech Industries was established in 2014 by Kibaran Resources and 3D Group to research and develop graphite and graphene applications for 3D printing . 3D Graphtech sources its graphite exclusively from Kibaran's Tanzanian graphite mine. Since its establishment, 3D Graphtech did not release any information and the company does not have a web page.

companies.name: 3DC
companies.description: 3DC is a Japan-based startup that aims to commercialize Graphene MesoSponge (GMS), a next-generation carbon material developed by the Nishihara Lab at the Advanced Institute for Materials Research of Tohoku University. “3DC” stands for “three-dimensional carbon materials,” based on GMS as a material expanded three-dimensionally from the two-dimensional graphene.

companies.name: Adisyn
companies.description: Adisyn is an ASX-listed company focused on harnessing the unique properties of graphene to develop an advanced semiconductor. Adisyn aims to develop its technology in partnership with some of the world’s largest semiconductor businesses and already possesses a strategic cooperation agreement with IMEC (the world’s leading semiconductor industry R&D hub). Adisyn is harnessing atomic layers of graphene to deliver a process for graphene-based interconnects, capable of improved performance and lower power consumption – delivered in an even smaller chip.

companies.name: AEH Innovative Hydrogel
companies.description: UK-based AEH Innovative Hydrogel Limited was established in 2018 to develop food-based fully recyclable hydroponic gel. AEH's hydrogel (branded as GelPonic) is graphene-based, and it is designed to reduce food production costs, improve quality and lower environmental impact.

companies.name: AERO MATERIALS
companies.description: Germany-based AERO MATERIALS uses a unique material, inspired by 'aero graphene' developed at Kiel University, made of over 99.9 % air. It's ultra-light, electrically conductive, mechanically resilient and scalable.

companies.name: Aerogel Core
companies.description: Aerogel Core has been established by University of Bath scientists, supported by Innovate UK funding. The Company specializes in ultra-light, graphene-based ‘aerogels’ that can be used for soundproofing and heat-shielding for the aerospace and automotive industries. The innovative and environmentally friendly aerogels are synthetic, porous materials manufactured by replacing the liquid component normally found in gels with gas.

companies.name: AlterBiota
companies.description: AlterBiota is a green chem-tech company that develops 'bio-graphene' additives designed to increase the strength of concrete and reduce its environmental footprint.

companies.name: Altered Carbon
companies.description: Altered Carbon (AC) was founded in 2018 in Bristol Robotics Laboratory, where the company is based.

companies.name: Amalyst
companies.description: UK-based Amalyst was established in 2012 to develop graphene-enhanced platinum-based fuel-cell catalysts. Amalyst is a full member of the Graphene Flagship.

companies.name: Anaphite
companies.description: Anaphite, located in the UK, aims to incorporate graphene into battery materials, via an inexpensive and scalable process that fits directly into existing cell production lines. The incorporation of graphene into Li-ion batteries is meant to improve battery life and charging times.

companies.name: Applied Nanotech
companies.description: Applied Nanotech is a PEN company and functions as the PEN Design Center focused on developing new products for the PEN family of companies using nanotechnology approaches. Its team of PhD level scientists and engineers works with companies to solve technical problems and create innovations, producing a competitive advantage for the PEN family. Applied Nanotech was founded in 1989, went public in 1993, and for the majority of its history focused on next generation display applications. However in late 2005, to diversify from one "make or break" technology, it expanded its focus to other areas leveraging its previous work. From 2006 to the present, it has made substantial progress in these ar

companies.name: Atomic Mechanics
companies.description: Atomic Mechanics is a limited company based in Manchester, founded in 2017. It has been created to design, manufacture and commercialize a range of sensor and actuator devices based on a patented graphene-based technology.

companies.name: Beijing Carbon Century Technology
companies.description: Beijing Carbon Century Technology, founded in 2013, specializes in graphene macro preparation technology, R&D and technical services of its downstream application technology. Beijing Century Carbon has been identified by the ISO9001 , ISO14001 certification, and passed the identification of high-tech enterprise.

companies.name: Black Semiconductor
companies.description: Black Semiconductor is a tech startup company based in Aachen, Germany. It was spun out of nonprofit research center AMO . Its goal is to manufacture and market extremely powerful microchips with integrated electronic-photonic circuits.

companies.name: Blacklidge
companies.description: Blacklidge is a U.S-based developer of asphalt products.

companies.name: Brain Scientific
companies.description: Brain Scientific is a New York City based medical device and technology company offering products and solutions related to the brain including neurology, AI, and machine learning. One of Brain Scientific's endeavors is a minimally invasive graphene electrode.

companies.name: Cambridge Raman Imaging (CRIL)
companies.description: Cambridge Raman Imaging Limited (CRIL) was registered in the UK in 2018. Its focus is on bringing to market high speed, label-free Raman imaging instruments. The first application uses graphene in medical imaging, aiming to deliver better patient outcomes through faster and more accurate tumor diagnosis and treatment.

companies.name: CamGraphIC
companies.description: CamGraphIC was spun out of Cambridge University to commercialize graphene photonic circuits technology for telecoms and datacoms. The company is supported by co-founder Frontier IP Group Plc.

companies.name: CAP-XX
companies.description: CAP-XX is a designer and manufacturer of thin, flat supercapacitors and energy management systems used in portable and small-scale electronic devices.

companies.name: Carbon Rivers
companies.description: Carbon Rivers is headquartered in Knoxville, TN.

companies.name: Carbon-Ion Energy
companies.description: Carbon-Ion Energy is a company that develops energy storage devices known as Carbon-Ion or C-Ion cells. It offers products for charging, discharging, and recyclable energy storage applications. The company serves clients in the transportation, industrial, and energy management sectors.

companies.name: Cemex
companies.description: Cemex is a leading sustainable construction materials and solutions company with innovation and sustainability at its core working to create value for its stakeholders. Cemex is a Mexican multinational company headquartered in San Pedro, Mexico.

companies.name: Cerebral Energy
companies.description: Cerebral Energy manufactures advanced energy systems and produces waste derived critical materials in the United States to enable rapid electrification of transport for long-term US energy independence.

companies.name: Chiral Nano
companies.description: Chiral Nano pioneers next-generation semiconductor and quantum technologies with nanomaterials, developing tools and processes for the scalable integration of nanomaterials into next-generation semiconductor devices. Founded in Switzerland in 2023 as an ETH Zurich spin-off, Chiral brings together expertise in nanotechnology, precision automation, and materials science to turn research into scalable industrial solutions.

companies.name: COnovate
companies.description: COnovate (previously called SafeLi) was founded on December 15, 2016 by Drs. Carol Hirschmugl and Marija Gajdardziska-Josifovska from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. A university-incubated startup, the company commercializes products based on a unique material called COPHITE (graphene monoxide), with an initial focus on Lithium Ion Batteries.

companies.name: CRX Coatings
companies.description: CRX Coatings is a Tennessee-based company that specializes in graphene-enhanced coatings. It supplies directly to customers through its distributing network. Among its products are coatings for marine applications, anti-fouling coatings and more.

companies.name: Deep Graphene
companies.description: Deep Graphene is an Israeli deep‑tech company developing advanced graphene‑based solutions for the electronics and semiconductor industries. The company focuses on multi‑layer graphene films and cooling modules that significantly improve heat spreading and thermal management in high‑power devices such as CPUs, GPUs, and advanced semiconductor packages.

companies.name: Divea
companies.description: Swiss clean technology company Divea was founded in 2024 as an EPFL spin-off, and is dedicated to the research and development of graphene filters.

companies.name: Dongxu Optoelectronic Technology
companies.description: Dongxu, also known as Tungshu, was established in 1997 and its headquarters and R&D center are located in Beijing. With roots in the optoelectronic display industry, it now has become a industrial investment enterprise focused on the optoelectronic display and renewable energy industries, while also covering financing, urbanization and real estate. The Tunghsu Group, with yearly revenues of over $5 Billion USD, has 40 subsidiaries under direct management with 100% share control or majority control, among which two are listed companies. Tunghsu Group has successively invested in and established over 20 production lines of flat panel display glass substrates and a production base for graphene,

companies.name: Dragon Elements
companies.description: Dragon Elements is a startup that aims to commercialize high-tech gadgets. It has developed LATIDO® capsules, a graphene-based technology designed to "redefine human interaction with hardware by eliminating the need for traditional audio and video components". Based in Valencia, Spain, Dragon Elements plans to enter various matrkets, such as audio, XR and more.

companies.name: Dreamfly Innovations
companies.description: Dreamfly Innovations (DFI) was founded in India in September 2021 by IIT and IISc Grads with 16 years of collective experience in the battery space.

companies.name: DZP Technologies
companies.description: DZP Technologies was founded in 2008 in the UK to develop specialty materials, formulations, and technologies for emerging industries. The Company works with its customers to create materials for a range of markets, from consumer electronics and wearables, to 3D-printing and renewable energy. DZP specializes in aqueous materials and formulations which are both user- and environmentally-friendly. Its materials provide a cost efficient alternative to conventional organic solvent systems which not only pose health risk to users, but also have hidden costs for solvent reclamation and health and safety compliance.

companies.name: Emberion
companies.description: Emberion, spun-off from Nokia's R&D unit, designs and develops high-performance optoelectronics based on graphene, other nanomaterials and CMOS integrated circuits. Emberion develops its own optoelectronics products, but also engages in technology licensing and can deliver integrated end products. Emberion has two R&D sites, one in Espoo Finland and one in Cambridge, UK. The company is a member of the European Graphene Flagship program.

companies.name: Emtel Energy
companies.description: Emtel Energy USA develops solid state graphene-based electrostatic storage solutions. Its Electrostatic Long-Duration Energy Storage (ELDES) offers a smart, safe, and more sustainable alternative to lithium. Emtel’s supercapacitor-based storage outperforms conventional solutions, ensuring reliability, efficiency, and long-term value.

companies.name: EnyGy
companies.description: EnyGy (formerly SupraG Energy) is an Australia-based company established in 2021 devoted to the development of graphene-based technologies to facilitate production of next generation energy storage solutions.

companies.name: Evercloak
companies.description: Evercloak is a Canada-based company that creates advanced material manufacturing processes that aim to solve environmental issues. With its membrane dehumidification technology, Evercloak aims to reduce the energy that air conditioners consume by more than 50%.

companies.name: Evove
companies.description: Evove, formerly called G2O Water, is a UK-based technology company that aims to "transform water globally and harvest suspended resources, creating abundance while helping to decarbonize our economies".

companies.name: FlexeGRAPH
companies.description: FlexeGRAPH was established in 2015 in Australia as a spin-out from ANU in Canberra to commercialize nanofluids for engines, electric vehicle batteries and computing cooling. FlexeGRAPH produces its own graphene and other 2D materials from raw materials using a proprietary method.

companies.name: FlexEnable
companies.description: FlexEnable develops OTFT-based backplanes for flexible displays, suitable for both EPD and OLED technologies. The company was spun-off from Plastic Logic in February 2015 to further develop the technology and license it for display makers.

companies.name: Freevolt
companies.description: Freevolt is a global company in the renewable energy sector, headquartered in California.

companies.name: Gerdau Graphene
companies.description: Gerdau Graphene, established in 2019 and owned by Gerdau, the largest steel producer in the Americas, is developing graphene based applications. Gerdau Graphene, a member of the University of Manchester's GEIC center, develops graphene-enhanced concrete, polymers, elastomers, lubricants, coatings and electronic sensors.

companies.name: GIGA Graphene Technologies (GGT)
companies.description: Giga Graphene Technologies specializes in the research, development, and application of graphene and other 2D advanced materials to make progress in diverse fields, from electronics to energy.

companies.name: Glenntex
companies.description: Sweden-based startup that has developed a method to functionalize graphene to reduce the need for virgin plastic in packaging by up to 30%. The Company's aim is to reduce virgin plastic consumption through smarter material design.

companies.name: Global Graphene Group (G3)
companies.description: Global Graphene Group (G3) develops, sells and licenses advanced graphene materials as well as graphene-enabled technologies for next-generation products such as phones, tires, paints, and electric vehicles.

companies.name: GMCC
companies.description: Established in 2011 in Wuxi, China, GMCC ELECTRONIC TECHNOLOGY WUXI develops and produces graphene-enhanced energy storage products. In 2015, following years of R&D, GMCC launched its first product, a graphene-enhanced super capacitor. GMCC currently offers single-cell capacitors, capacitor modules and capacitor management systems.

companies.name: Grafine
companies.description: UK-based Grafine was established by two University of Manchester academics, to develop innovative high-performance rubbers, elastomers and other such soft materials enhanced with graphene. Beyond its materials, Grafine is offering a range of technical development services to manufacturing companies.

companies.name: Grafren
companies.description: Sweden-based Grafren develops smart textiles using its patented method to separate high-quality graphene flakes. Grafren was spun off from Linkoping University, Sweden, in 2018.

companies.name: GRAFTA Nanotech
companies.description: GRAFTA Nanotech is a Canada-based company that leverages the nanoscale structure of graphene to act as an adsorbent and capture water contaminants. Some of these contaminants are heavy metals, organic molecules, and even inorganic substances like ammonia.

companies.name: Grahope New Materials
companies.description: Xiwang Grahope New Materials (GNM) focuses on the R&D of graphene heating technology and the development of graphene products in general. It has created patented technology of graphene heating film and filed over 100 invention patents. GNM was founded by Professor Feng Guanping, who is a Chinese graphene industry pioneer, honorary president of Jiangnan Graphene Research Institute, and president of the Shenzhen Graphene Association. GNM has four R&D subsidiaries, in Shenzhen, Shanghai, Wuxi and Changzhou.

companies.name: Granode Materials
companies.description: Granode Materials develops a method for producing a new graphene-based anode material for lithium-ion batteries. These batteries are meant to be cheaper and lighter with better storage capacity, creating a more sustainable alternative to today's lithium-ion batteries. Granode Materials received its investment in 2021, when it was spun out of 2D Fab. A rights issue of 12 million SEK (around USD$1,327,000) was carried out. The funds were designated for product development and marketing. Investors include former head of SEB, Lars Thunell, and Almi Invest.

companies.name: GraphAudio
companies.description: GraphAudio was established in 2016 to commercialize graphene-based acoustic products. GraphAudio's technology originated from UC Berkeley and Berkeley Lab. GraphAudio uses a 100% graphene driver to function as either an electrostatic speaker or a microphone-ultrasonic sensor. GraphAudio says it will launch graphene headphones and amplifiers as early as in 2022.

companies.name: Grapheal
companies.description: Grapheal was spun-off from the Neel Institute CNRS Grenoble in 2019 to commercialize graphene-based medical patches that actively stimulates wound healing.

companies.name: Graphenaton Technologies
companies.description: Graphenaton Technologies is a Switzerland-based company that develops graphene applications like heating, energy storage, and energy production.

companies.name: Graphene Composites
companies.description: Graphene Composites Limited (GC) is a nano-materials technology company that makes use of graphene, aerogels and other materials to produce a range of composites.

companies.name: Graphene ESD
companies.description: Graphene ESD was established in 2014 in the US with an aim to develop graphene-based Super Capacitor technology developed by Graphene Laboratories and Stony Brook University .

companies.name: Graphene Green Concrete (GGC)
companies.description: Graphene Green Concrete (GGC) is a UK-based company with links to the University of Manchester. Its goal is to reduce the carbon footprint of infrastructures by producing concrete using 100% recycled aggregates instead of natural aggregates, without compromising strength & durability.

companies.name: Graphene Innovations Manchester (GIM)
companies.description: Graphene Innovations Manchester (GIM) is a Manchester-based deep-tech company that develops and commercializes graphene-enhanced materials and products in partnership with industrial clients.

companies.name: Graphenea
companies.description: Graphenea, a technology company founded in 2010, is a leading graphene producer. Graphenea focuses on contributing to the successful development of Graphene applications of its customers, in a wide range of sectors and in more than 60 countries in the world. Through research and innovation, it supports its customers with a portfolio consisting of: CVD Graphene films, Graphene Field-Effect-Transistors chips (GFETs), Graphene Foundry Services (GFAB) and Graphene Oxides. Graphenea’s facilities are located in Spain (San Sebastián) and USA (Boston).

companies.name: GrapheneDx
companies.description: GrapheneDX is a diagnostics startup, developing a graphene-based technology for at-home testing. It is designing a platform technology that will enable better and faster health management that will provide results in under five minutes. Its proprietary technology(under development) aims to reach accuracy on par with most advanced diagnostics technologies.

companies.name: Graphenemex
companies.description: Graphenemex was established in 2016 in Mexico with an aim to become a high quality graphene producer and applications developer. The company currently produces both graphene flakes, graphene oxide, reduced graphene oxide and CVD graphene. Graphenemex's current capacity for graphene flakes and GO is about one ton per year.

companies.name: GraphEnergyTech
companies.description: GraphEnergyTech developed and patented a novel process to integrate graphene electrodes into solar cells, replacing the silver and other precious metals whilst retaining or improving power conversion efficiencies and reliability. It is now working with partners to scale this technology and bring the cost and performance benefits to all types of solar cell.

companies.name: GrapheneUP
companies.description: GrapheneUP is a private and independent graphene company based in the Czech Republic, focusing on the bulk production of few-layer graphene and the development and commercialization of graphene-based additives, dispersions, masterbatches.

companies.name: Graphenglass
companies.description: Graphenglass is a Spain-based company that is focused on transferring the high performance of graphene to known materials.

companies.name: GraphenicaLab
companies.description: GraphenicaLab is a Spain-based company, spun off company from the Catalan Institute of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology (ICN2) with a patented technology to print flexible graphene sensors and electronic devices on any surface.

companies.name: Graphenix
companies.description: Graphenix is a Thailand-based company that specializes in lifestyle products, with an emphasis on using scientific innovation to improve health, comfort, and everyday lifestyle products. It uses graphene to make textiles and products such as bankets, clothing and more.

companies.name: Graphenory
companies.description: Graphenory was established in 2024 based on technology out of Keio University. The company is working on graphene-based optical devices like small infrared light sources that can operate on a chip. Graphenory aims to commercialize chip-based infrared light sources and infrared analyzers that utilize them, such as high spatial resolution infrared analyzers.

companies.name: Graphex Technologies
companies.description: Graphex Technologies develops energy-efficient storage solutions, based on its proprietary graphene-based products - mainly its spherical graphite. Graphex is developing Li-Ion batteries that utilize its spherical graphite.

companies.name: Graphite Innovation and Technologies
companies.description: Graphite Innovation and Technologies (GIT) is a Canada-based materials engineering startup focused on delivering disruptive uses for graphene technologies.

companies.name: Graphmatech
companies.description: Graphmatech is a Swedish graphene materials technology company that develops novel graphene-based nanocomposite materials and products. Graphmatech focuses on three main business areas - metal-graphene composites and coated powders, polymer-graphene composites and additives for energy storage. In January 2017 Graphmatech reported a breakthrough made at the Division of Inorganic Chemistry at Uppsala University, Sweden , designing and manufacturing a graphene hybrid material with a cleverly designed microstructure.

companies.name: GraphWear
companies.description: GraphWear is a startup that is developing a graphene-based sweatpatch that detects important biometric data in real-time. It can analyze sweat and communicate its findings via mobile app. It could tell, among other things, when a person needs to drink water in order to prevent a muscle cramp.

companies.name: Green Graphene
companies.description: US-based Green Graphene was established in 2015, to produce Graphene Oxide and r-GO materials using an environmentally-friendly process.

companies.name: Green Tech
companies.description: China-based Green Tech is a Supercapacitors developer, established in 2002. The company produces a wide range of supercapacitors, from single-cell units to large systems.

companies.name: GRIP Molecular Technologies
companies.description: US-based GRIP Molecular Technologies develops in-house diagnostic test that is based on a single-use bio-sensor. The sensor contains CVD graphene. GRIP Molecular raised $3 million in 2021 and is on track for a commercial launch in 2025.

companies.name: Hainan Weishi New Energy Technology
companies.description: Hainan Weishi New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. is a China‑based energy storage company focusing on advanced battery technologies that incorporate graphene materials. The company develops and manufactures energy storage equipment with an emphasis on fast‑charging graphene batteries and graphene carbon composite battery systems, targeting improved charge rates, cycle life and overall energy efficiency compared to conventional chemistries.

companies.name: Hangzhou Gaoxi Technology
companies.description: Hangzhou GaoXi Technology Co., Ltd. was founded in 2016 and is recognized as a national-level specialized and innovative "little giant" enterprise, a national high-tech enterprise, and a member unit of the National Graphene Innovation Center.

companies.name: Hawkeye Bio
companies.description: Hawkeye Bio is a biotechnology company developing advanced biosensor technologies for the early detection and monitoring of disease. By integrating innovations in materials science, nanotechnology, and molecular diagnostics, Hawkeye Bio is producing highly sensitive diagnostic tests capable of detecting early biological signals associated with cancer and inflammatory disorders.

companies.name: Hefei Haizhou New Material SuperC
companies.description: China-based Hefei Haizhou New Material, also known as SuperC, develops and manufactures nano-materials. The Company develops Few Layer Graphene materials (FLG), enabling the production of lithium ion batteries, fireproof coatings, anticorrosive coatings, electrical and thermal conductivity materials, and graphene composite materials.

companies.name: Hememics
companies.description: US-based Hememics is commercializing a patented rapid handheld bio testing platform, to bring lab-quality results on a mobile device. The company's platform is based on a unique graphene-based sensor that can detect molecular, antigens and antibody targets from a single sample.

companies.name: HexagonFab
companies.description: UK-based HexagonFab develops biological sensors based on graphene. The company is a spin-off from the University of Cambridge. HexagonFab offers sensors including handheld readout devices to analyze protein concentrations and interactions. The company says its graphene-based sensor offer highly sensitive results in an affordable and portable device.

companies.name: Hollowgraf
companies.description: Hollowgraf Ltd develops solutions for sustainable and circular water desalination using membranes and processes that transform seawater into clean water and valuable products—without applied hydraulic pressure, draw solutions and generating brine.

companies.name: Huvis
companies.description: Korea-based Huvis was established in 2000, when SK Chemicals and Samyang Corporation established it by combining their advanced technology with state-of-the-art production capabilities.

companies.name: HyCarb
companies.description: HyCarb is a Florida-based early-stage company, headquartered at the University of Central Florida Business Incubator in Research Park. HyCarb uses graphene and carbon nanotubes to develop enhanced, environmentally-friendly batteries, super-capacitors, fuel cells, solar panels, sensors, catalysts, filters and transistors. HyCarb has an exclusive license for three patents from the University of Central Florida (UCF) that utilize graphene aerogels and conducting polymers. HyCarb is currently focused on creating five new anodes and five new cathodes to be fabricated into prototype batteries that store renewable energy.

companies.name: Iceni Labs
companies.description: Iceni Labs is a spin-out from Imperial College London, developing a graphene-based microphone.
