The new graphene microphones will provide higher audio quality than existing technologies as the potential of graphene as a microphone diaphragm is well known, as the stresses and strains across the membrane are more uniform than in a silicon device.

companies.name: IdentifySensors
companies.description: IdentifySensors Biologics is developing and expanding an extensive diagnostic platform intended to rapidly detect a wide range of infectious pathogens and cancerous biomarkers through solid-state digital biosensors that connect to the cloud.

companies.name: iGii
companies.description: Scotland-based iGii (formerly: Integrated Graphene and before that RD Graphene) is an advanced materials company who has invented, patented and commercialized a design for manufacture process to produce high performing pure 3D Graphene Foam, Gii, on any surface, in seconds.

companies.name: Imagine Intelligent Materials
companies.description: Imagine Intelligent Materials is an Australian developer of graphene-based coatings for industrial textiles and fibres. The coatings solutions are delivered as masterbatch and can be used to deliver new functionalities in geotextiles, geogrids, and geomembranes.

companies.name: INBRAIN Neuroelectronics
companies.description: INBRAIN Neuroelectronics is a Spain-based company that develop high density and high resolution graphene intelligent neural systems for central and peripheral Neuroelectronic applications.

companies.name: INNANO
companies.description: INNANO develops graphene-enabled technologies for next-generation protective coatings. The company engineers nanocoating solutions that modify and protect surfaces, improving durability, and extending service life while lowering maintenance requirements in demanding operating environments. INNANO has established its operations at Exeter Science Park as it prepares for the next stage of its growth and international expansion.

companies.name: Ionic Industries
companies.description: Australia-based Ionic Industries (formerly known as Grafitech) was spun-off from Strategic Energy Resources (SER) in 2015 with an aim to develop graphene-based technologies. Ionic develops graphene-based supercapacitors , membranes and sand-coated sand for water treatment and chemical separation.

companies.name: Ipower Batteries
companies.description: Ipower is an India-based manufacturer of Lithium batteries for electric vehicles.

companies.name: JNC Materials
companies.description: JNC Materials is a Korea-based battery company that specializes in secondary battery materials, battery pack materials, and electronic materials, like with silicon heat dissipation materials. The Company uses a unique reduced graphene/silicon mass production process.

companies.name: JTX
companies.description: JTX (officially Shandong Prosperous Star Optoelectronics Co), established in May 2014 in China, is a developer of LED based lighting products. JTX has over 800 employees and is involved with all the LED lighting value chain, from LED chips and filaments to complete light bulbs. In July 2016 JTX announced plans to merge with Graphene Lighting PLC , but these plans were later cancelled .

companies.name: Kivoro
companies.description: KIVORO was spun-off of Graphenea in late 2022. It will serve as a specialty chemicals company, to commercialize various current industrial solutions and also move beyond graphene. It will maintain its leading expertise in carbon and nanomaterials, but also focused on developing specialty chemicals for clients.

companies.name: Kovalent Coatings
companies.description: Australia-based Kovalent Coatings pioneers advanced ceramic formulations for automotive, marine, and aviation industries. Among its products are several graphene-based coating products.

companies.name: Kukil Graphene
companies.description: Founded in 2018, Kukil Graphene is mainly involved in graphene composites and CVD-based materials. Kukil Graphene is owned by KUKIL Paper, a leader in the field of specialized paper materials using natural and synthetic fibers. Expanding its business to graphene will let it focus on graphene thin films using direct transfer CVD technologies with low temperature and more.

companies.name: LayerLogic
companies.description: LayerLogic is a Swedish deeptech startup, spun out of Chalmers University of Technology, that harnesses graphene-enhanced biosensing technology for rapid, precise bacteria detection.

companies.name: Linktop
companies.description: Linktop is a China-based developer and manufacturer of smart wearables and telehealth devices. Founded in 2003 and headquartered in Xiamen, Fujian Province, the company also operates offices in the US and Europe and supplies its products globally to medical providers, telehealth platforms and consumer wellness brands.

companies.name: Log 9 Materials
companies.description: Log 9 Materials was established in 2015 as an IIT Roorkee spin-off to focus on graphene material production and application development.

companies.name: Lomiko Metals
companies.description: Lomiko Metals Inc. (TSXV:LMR, OTCQX:LMRMF, FSE:DH8B) is a Canada-based junior miner at the exploration-stage. Lomiko is invested in graphene technologies through Graphene 3D Labs and Graphene ESD .

companies.name: Lyten
companies.description: Lyten is a privately held advanced materials company founded in 2015, based in San Jose, California. Lyten developed Lyten 3D Graphene, a patented library of materials that has enabled the company to develop various solutions in the fields of energy storage, composite systems, and chemical & passive sensors.

companies.name: Maxvolt Energy Industries
companies.description: Established in 2019, Maxvolt Energy Industries Limited is an India-based manufacturer & supplier of Lithium battery packs for all type of Electric Vehicles.

companies.name: MCR Safety
companies.description: MCR Safety manufactures and supplies PPE such as work gloves and safety glasses. The Company has offices and distribution centers in the UK, Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia. The Company started out in 1953 when Parmelee Ltd was established in the UK to manufacture eye protection.

companies.name: Medica
companies.description: Medica S.p.a. is an Italian company that produces filters based on hollow fiber membranes for various applications, ranging from blood purification to water filtration. Medica is a partner of the Graphene Flagship and is working to integrate graphene in water filters as part of the Spearheard Project Graphil.

companies.name: MITO Material Solutions
companies.description: MITO Material Solutions is a U.S-based nano-additive solutions provider. Its proprietary graphene functionalization technique allows it to make hybrid polymer modifiers for use in all industries.

companies.name: NanoAffix Science
companies.description: NanoAffix Science is a spin-off small business formed around exclusively licensed patented technologies from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee Research Foundation.

companies.name: NanoGraf
companies.description: NanoGraf, formerly known as SiNode Systems, was established in 2013 to commercial a novel anode Li-ion battery technology developed at Northwestern University. SiNode's anode uses a composite material of silicon nano-particles and graphene in a layered structure.

companies.name: Nanophyll
companies.description: Canada-based NanoPhyll develops and manufacturs coatings, with a focus on anti-corrosive and anti-fouling coatings.

companies.name: Nanotech Energy
companies.description: Nanotech Energy is a U.S-based supplier of graphene and graphene oxide materials a

companies.name: NematiQ
companies.description: NematiQ is a 100%-owned subsidiary of Clean TeQ Water (ASX:CNQ), and is headquartered in Melbourne, Australia. It aims to commercialize its graphene membrane filtration technology.

companies.name: NEO Battery Materials
companies.description: NEO Battery Materials Ltd. (TSXV: NBM) (OTC: NBMFF) is a Canada-based resource company focused on silicon materials for lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles. The Company is focusing on developing silicon anode materials through unique nanocoating layers.

companies.name: NexGen Heating
companies.description: NexGen is a UK-based graphite and graphene based nano-technology developer, that provides an innovative heating solution for applications across multiple industry sectors. The Company's low resistance heating films are used in their heated wallpaper tech and additional solutions for floors and ceilings.

companies.name: NexTech Batteries
companies.description: NexTech Batteries is a U.S-based battery company, founded in 2016 with exclusive Li-S technology licensure from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL).

companies.name: Nova Graphene Ballistics
companies.description: Nova Graphene Ballistics, Inc. (OTC PINK: BIEI), (formerly 'Premier Biomedical Inc.'), is a global advanced materials firm with a focus on research, production and marketing of proprietary CarbonEra™ graphene. The Company is currently in pursuit of its first initiative - 3D-printed Graphene Ballistic Plate Production, including the prototype, with regard to novel graphene production.

companies.name: ONE Condoms
companies.description: Established in 2004, ONE Condoms is a socially-conscious company dedicated to promoting sexual health awareness, sustainability, and inclusivity. Known for award-winning, premium condoms and lubricants, ONE brings a unique perspective to sexual health by combining sustainable product design, manufacturing innovation, and community engagement.

companies.name: ORA
companies.description: ORA is a Canada-based company that is said to use GO to design loudspeakers and headphones. The company claims that these GO-enhanced audio components boast a better sound quality, as well as enhanced efficiency and smaller/lighter form factors.

companies.name: Paragraf
companies.description: UK-based Paragraf was spun-off from the Centre for Gallium Nitride group of Professor Sir Colin Humphreys in the Department of Materials Science at the University of Cambridge to commercialize graphene-based electronic devices. Paragraf serves the sensor, energy and semiconductor markets. The company produces single-layer graphene (and other 2D materials) materials that are compatible with existing electronic device manufacturing production processes. In 2025, Paragraf raised $55 million to expand graphene chip production .

companies.name: Paragraf USA (Cardea Bio)
companies.description: San Diego-based Cardea Bio, previously called Nanomedical Diagnostics , turned into Paragraf USA when it was bought by UK-based Paragraf in May 2023.

companies.name: Plaid Technologies
companies.description: Plaid Technologies focuses on the development and commercialization of graphene-enhanced concrete technology. Its business includes refining proprietary technology for the uniform dispersion of graphene in cement, and advancing a patent application related to the production of expanded graphite for industrial use.

companies.name: Pleione Energy
companies.description: Pleione Energy S.A is an International Joint Venture between the Greek company ADAMANT COMPOSITES and the German company OMNIDEA-RTG. The company was established in 2015 and is located in Athens, Greece. It is part of the New Science & Technology Park of Attica â€œLefkipposâ€ of the National Center for Scientific Research (NCSR) "Demokritos".

companies.name: PolyJoule
companies.description: PolyJoule is a spin-off of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). The Boston-based energy storage company is developing conductive polymer battery technology using graphene. PolyJoule develops devices based on a standard, two-electrode electrochemical cell containing conductive polymers, a carbon-graphene hybrid, and a non-flammable liquid electrolyte.

companies.name: Prognomics
companies.description: Prognomics LTD was established in 2014 as a spin-out company from Swansea University, UK, with an aim to develop graphene-based sensors. The company develops a number of methods to graft bio-receptors (for example, antibodies) to graphene in order to get sensitive and selective detection.

companies.name: Promethient
companies.description: Promethient was founded in 2012 by Charles Cauchy, an expert in the field of solid state heating and cooling using thermoelectric devices. Promethientâs solid state heating and cooling technology is marketed under the Thermavance brand name.

companies.name: Purafy Clean Technologies
companies.description: Purafy Clean Technologies is a division of Grafoid Inc., a graphene research, development and investment company that invests in, manages and develops markets for processes that produce economically scalable graphene for use in graphene development applications by leading corporations and institutions.

companies.name: Quantag Nanotechnologies
companies.description: Turkey-based Quantag Nanotechnologies was established in 2014 to develop advanced tagging technologies. The company is basing its tagging materials on graphene quantum dots combined with ultra-sensitive sensors.

companies.name: Qurv Technologies
companies.description: Qurv Technologies, based in Barcelona, Spain, is a startup established in 2020 developing wide-spectrum image sensors based on graphene and quantum-dot technologies.

companies.name: Real Graphene
companies.description: Real Graphene is a U.S-based technology company working on graphene-enhanced battery cells. Founded by two UC Berkeley graduates who realized graphene's potential lab research, the Company's goal is to integrate graphene into affordable every day technology.

companies.name: SalgenX
companies.description: Salgenx is focused on developing and commercializing advanced salt water flow battery technology. Salgenx aims to revolutionize the energy storage industry by offering high-performance grid-scale batteries that not only provide reliable power but also deliver additional benefits such as desalination and graphene production.

companies.name: SEEDS
companies.description: SEEDS stands for Sustainable Energy Efficient Designed Structures. The company develops energy generation solutions by formulating printable inks using advanced carbon based nano-structures (presumably graphene). These are formed into bespoke auxiliary power systems to support power demands.

companies.name: Shanghai Kyorene New Material Technology
companies.description: Shanghai Kyorene New Material Technology has developed a graphene fiber for integration in textiles. The technology is said to make graphene completely integrated with high polymer materials under room temperature, and adds special function to ordinary textile products like antibacterial, ultraviolet-proof, anti-static and heat preservation effects.

companies.name: SHT (Smart High Tech)
companies.description: Smart High Tech is a Swedish company focused on producing new heat-dissipating materials reinforced with graphene with a focus on cooling of CPUs, GPUs, Chiplets and other heat-intensive electronics devices.

companies.name: Sicona Battery Technologies
companies.description: Sicona leverages low cost and abundant silicon metal to develop next-gen battery materials.

companies.name: Skeleton Technologies
companies.description: Skeleton Technologies is a developer and manufacturer of high energy and power density ultracapacitors. The company provides green and cost-effective energy storage solutions for the automotive, transportation, industrial and renewable energy markets.

companies.name: SmartIR
companies.description: SmartIR is a spinout company from the University of Manchester that is developing a cost-effective graphene-based solution that will ensure satellites can control thermal radiation on demand.

companies.name: Solidion Technology
companies.description: Solidion Technology, an advanced battery technology company, aims to address the issue of battery materials supply shortage, driven by anticipated soaring demand for electric vehicle (EV) and energy storage systems (ESS) battery capacities.

companies.name: SoundCell
companies.description: SoundCell is a spin-off of (Graphene Flagship partner) TU Delft that offers a diagnostic device for determining cell viability based on the minute vibrations caused by living cells. The diagnostic device is capable of AST testing within hours rather than days. SoundCell's device measures nanoscale motion from living cells with graphene membranes and is not limited by the growth rate.

companies.name: SPAC
companies.description: SPAC SpA is an Italy-based medium-sized enterprise with expertise in producing high-performance, technical textiles for automotive, upholstery, sports applications and other sectors. Founded in 1973, SPAC has a production plant for coated polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polyurethane (PU), and a division for the lamination of technical textiles.

companies.name: SpaceBlue
companies.description: SpaceBlue invented and developed a graphene-enhanced recycled rubber floor mat to address the global problem of waste tyre, currently being burned or going to landfill. SpaceBlue is a Manchester-based start-up (started with the support of the Graphene Engineering Innovation Centre at the University of Manchester) that came up with a novel solution to address the waste tyre issue by developing a graphene-enhanced recycled rubber product- the SpaceMat. It is said by the company to be the best option to replace synthetic mat, disposal of which is a cause of pollution leading to an environmental disaster.

companies.name: Sparc Technologies
companies.description: Sparc Technologies (ASX:SPN) is a South Australian based company that is focusing on the development of innovative technology solutions using graphene.

companies.name: Surwon Technology
companies.description: Surwon Technology is a Hong Kong based advanced materials company that specializes on graphene applications.

companies.name: Sustainable Energy Technologies (SETI)
companies.description: Sustainable Energy Technologies (SETI) was founded to bring next generation energy storage solutions to business and consumers alike. The Company’s signature product is the SETI Power Pack, an energy storage solution that is a hybrid graphene/lithium-ion supercapacitor intended to replace the need for traditional batteries.

companies.name: Tachmed
companies.description: Tachmed is a UK-based company that developed a digital diagnostics device based on graphene biosensors to test for various different conditions, including COVID-19 and flu.

companies.name: Talga Resources
companies.description: Talga Resources Ltd is a multi-national company focused on graphite mining and graphene supply and application development. The company mines graphite in Sweden, operates a test processing facility in Germany under Talga Advanced Materials GmbH and has a product development arm, Talga Technologies UK Ltd located in Cambridge, UK.

companies.name: Tata Steel
companies.description: Tata group is a multinational enterprise, headquartered in India, that includes over 100 independent operating companies. Tata Steel is considered as Tata Group's flagship company and is one of the leading steel producers in the world. Tata Steel has been active in the field of graphene R&D for many years, with work that ranges from steel-related projects back in 2014 , through releasing a graphene-based product range - the Tiscon Superlinks+ graphene-coated stirrups in 2017, to ongoing development and commercialization work.

companies.name: The Graphene Solution
companies.description: The Graphene Solution is a materials technology company based in Houston, Texas, that specializes in graphene-enhanced concrete designed to improve strength, durability, and sustainability in construction projects.

companies.name: Theragnostic Technologies
companies.description: Theragnostic Technologies was established in 2012 as a spin-off from Stony Brook University to develop a new efficient graphene-based MRI contrast agent that is safer and cheaper than current gadolinium-based agents.

companies.name: TLC Products
companies.description: TLC has developed a commercial production process, licensed from Rutgers University, to produce graphene composites. TLC's unique process mixes graphite directly with the resin to make graphene composites, claiming to "break the cost barrier for using graphene in plastics".

companies.name: Toraphene
companies.description: Toraphene is a UK-based biotechnology and materials company aiming to replace single-use plastic packaging with its alternative: Toraphene. Toraphene is a biodegradable, compostable & commercially-viable plastic packaging substitute, that embeds graphene platelets in the natural polymers. It is said by the Company to be stronger, thinner & to give better food protection than alternatives.

companies.name: Triera Biosciences
companies.description: Triera Biosciences is a wholly owned subsidiary of Zentek Ltd. Through advancements in next-generation materials like graphene and other innovative developments, Zentek is discovering new ways to protect against pathogens, detect and treat disease, make building materials stronger, and produce cleaner energy. Triera Biosciences is pioneering a transformative aptamer platform with potential for development of new treatments. Preclinical trials have demonstrated efficacy that have matched or exceeded monoclonal antibodies.

companies.name: True 2 Materials
companies.description: True 2 Materials relies on a simple, high speed manufacturing process (patents pending) that enables production of large, substrate independent graphene and graphene oxide films. Volume production and specific tuning of the films will make it possible for the company's partners to bring graphene and GO based products to commercial markets across multiple industries. The company uses proprietary methodology to make its own graphene. From this graphene powder it make its own inks, paints, resins etc. The company also produces substrate-free films, meaning they are not on copper, or silicon etc. These are, according to the company, less than 10 atoms thick films that are free of any substrate.

companies.name: Trustwell
companies.description: Chengdu Trustwell New Material (Trustwell), based in China develops and manufactures polymers for the printing, tire and rubber industries. In October 2015 Trustwell unveiled a new technology (originally from Sichuan University Polymers Institute) that manages to mix graphene flakes into rubber specifically for tire applications. The company produces its own graphene flakes.

companies.name: Vaulta
companies.description: Vaulta is a battery casing technology company based in Brisbane, Australia. Vaulta has developed a lighter and smaller battery case with fewer parts, creating scalable efficiencies and opportunities for manufacturers. Vaulta uses graphene as a critical part of its design.

companies.name: Vesi Water
companies.description: Vesi Water develops smart and sustainable solutions to the water industry. It is utilizing proprietary graphene-oxide based technology developed in collaboration with the University of New South Wales to harvest fresh water from airborne humidity, creating fresh water where none exists.

companies.name: Via Separations
companies.description: MIT spinoff Via Separations develops graphene oxide membranes. Cost-effective and robust, the membranes aim to reduce the amount of energy used in industrial separations by 90 percent.

companies.name: Vitrotem
companies.description: Vitrotem, based in the Netherlands, was founded in 2019 to improve the fundamental understanding of life by unlocking the power of electron microscopy to the analysis of biological materials and processes in liquid water, the native environment of biology.

companies.name: Vocxi Health
companies.description: Vocxi Health is a diagnostic startup focused on transforming early disease detection through breath-based testing, anchored in its proprietary MyBreathPrint® technology. Originating from more than a decade of collaboration between a global medical device company and a world-class research institution, the company was formally incorporated in 2022 to bring a noninvasive, highly sensitive breath sensor to market.

companies.name: Volexion
companies.description: Volexion is a startup commercializing a unique graphene technology for the next generation of Li-ion battery materials. Its first product is a drop-in high energy cathode material with a reported 10x better performance than state of the art, moving the Li-ion and electric vehicle industry 10 years forward.

companies.name: Volfpack Energy
companies.description: Volfpack Energy is a Sri Lanka-based company focused on renewable energy storage, said to be "leveraging advanced supercapacitor, battery, and software technologies" to offer "integrated solutions to combat the intermittent challenges of solar and wind power, ensuring consistent energy storage and delivery".

companies.name: Vorbeck Materials
companies.description: Vorbeck Materials is a U.S-based company that manufactures its own graphene materials (Vor-x®), conductive inks (Vor-ink™), and high-performance electronic components for advanced applications.

companies.name: Watercycle Technologies
companies.description: Watercycle Technologies is a spin-out from The University of Manchester that uses graphene-based membranes and systems to extract lithium and other minerals from brines and water solutions. Using its patented membrane technology, the Company's solutions extract lithium, minerals and other metals from diverse water sources including groundwater, industrial, municipal and agricultural wastewater and seawater.

companies.name: Wuxi Graphene Film
companies.description: Wuxi Graphene Film, based in the Huishan Economic Development Zone in Wuxi, is producing graphene-based touch films. The company is held by Xiwang Grahope New Materials (70%) and The Sixth Elements Materials (30%).

companies.name: Yadea
companies.description: Yadea Group is an electric two-wheeler manufacturer integrating the development, production and sales of pedelec, electric mopeds, electric motorcycles, electric kick scooters and their accessories. Yadea has launched the Graphene 3.0 Battery, and the new Champion Series 2.0 E8 vehicles that are said to be equipped with the graphene batteries.

companies.name: Znshine Solar
companies.description: ZNShine Solar is a maker of PV modules, PV power station and EPC, founded in 1988 in China. In May 2018, ZNShine Solar launched the G12 evolution era series - a 12-busbar graphene module, 5-busbar graphene module and double-glass graphene module.

companies.name: Zoxcell
companies.description: Zoxcell, based in Hong Kong with operations in Pakistan and Dubai, produces graphene-enhanced supercapacitors. Zoxcell is serving the automotive, industrial, consumer electronics, telecom and transportation markets, and it offers a wide range of supercapacitors, produced in Pakistan and China.

companies.name: Aixtron
companies.description: Aixtron SE is a provider of deposition equipment to the semiconductor industry. The company's technology solutions are used to build advanced components for electronic and opto-electronic applications based on compound, silicon, or organic semiconductor materials.

companies.name: Annealsys
companies.description: Annealsys is a manufacturer of Rapid Thermal Processing (RTP) and Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) systems. The company's systems offer multi-process capabilities in the same reactor, and besides graphene production units, the company also offers DLI-CVD system solutions for MoS 2 deposition.

companies.name: CVD Equipment
companies.description: CVD Equipment Corporation (a US-based company) offers a variety of process and support equipment for both R&D and production facilities. CVD Equipment offers graphene production systems.

companies.name: Destination 2D
companies.description: Destination 2D is a startup focuses on the integration of graphene interconnects into standard CMOS semiconductor process technology at scale and without the traditional issues that have prevented graphene from being used in chip manufacturing processes to date.

companies.name: DrM
companies.description: DrM Ag (Dr. Mueller), based in Switzerland, is a manufacturer of technically sophisticated filtration systems for solid/liquid separation for use in processing industries, with over 3,000 installations worldwide.

companies.name: Loginns
companies.description: Loginns has a patented exfoliation process which it uses to make equipment that produces graphene via exfoliation. Its prominent line seems to be called the AT800 series.

companies.name: Microfluidics
companies.description: Microfluidics designs and manufactures high pressure, high shear fluid processors. The company's Microfluidizer are used for liquid exfoliation of graphite to produce graphene. Microfluidics offers an entire product line ranges from lab scale to large production scale.

companies.name: Moorfield
companies.description: Moorfield is a UK based company, founded in 1989 that designs and manufacture a wide range of R&D-scale laboratory systems. The company focuses on vacuum deposition products and CVD synthesis.

companies.name: MTI Corporation
companies.description: MTI Corporation, based in California US, was established in 1994 and is a leading manufacturer of oxide crystals and substrates. The company also offers lab equipment and furnaces - and they have a range of tube furnaces for graphene growth.

companies.name: Oxford Instruments
companies.description: Oxford Instruments is a leading provider of high technology tools and systems for research and industry. The company designs and manufactures equipment that can fabricate, analyse and manipulate matter at the atomic and molecular level, including CVD equipment for graphene production and various systems for metrology and testing.

companies.name: Picosun
companies.description: Picosun, based in Espoo Finland, was established in 2004 to develop Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) reactors for micro- and nanotechnology applications. The company is developing ALD-based graphene deposition using its advanced PEALD (plasma-enhanced ALD) system.

companies.name: planarTECH
companies.description: Established in 2014, PlanarTECH is a UK-based company (with manufacturing in Korea) that offers both R&D and production-scale equipment, analytical equipment and training services for all classes of emerging 2D materials (graphene, boron nitride, molybdenum disulfide, etc.) as well as other carbon-based materials such as CNTs and CVD diamond (both R&D and mass production).

companies.name: Scienta Omicron
companies.description: Scienta Omicron was established in 2017 as a merger between two Surface Science companies - VG Scienta and Omicron NanoTechnology. For graphene (and other 2D materials), the company offers VG Scienta's CVD deposition system, in addition to PVD and sputtering systems based on metal evaporation using thermal cells or E beam.

companies.name: SECO/WARWICK
companies.description: The SECO/WARWICK Group a multinational heat processing furnace and equipment provider. The company is a full service manufacturer, providing engineering, research & development, manufacturing, turnkey installation, commissioning and aftermarket service. For the graphene market, the company offers GraphMaster, CVD reactors for large-format graphene production.

companies.name: Veeco
companies.description: Veeco Instruments is making process equipment for several markets. The company's main business segments are LEDs (and OLEDs ), PVs and data storage. Veeco supplies Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) products which can be used for graphene deposition.

companies.name: Alabama Graphite
companies.description: Alabama Graphite, a Canadian based company, is conducting graphite exploration and development at two graphite mines in Alabama, USA.Â In March 2015, Alabama Graphite announced that it has found naturally occurring flake graphene at its Coosa Property in Alabama, USA . The company found several graphene types: few-layer graphene (2-5 layers), multi-layer graphene (2-10 layers), and graphite nanoplates (less than 100 nm thick).

companies.name: American Graphite Technologies
companies.description: American Graphite Technologies (AGT) is a mineral exploration and technology development company. AGT has 100% ownership of 100 mineral claims in Quebec, Canada (close by to Focus Graphite's proven graphite resource ).

companies.name: Anson Resources
companies.description: Anson Resources (previously known as Mayan Iron Corporation) is a Western Australian based mining exploration company that was formed in 2009 and listed on the ASX in July 2010. The companyâs primary goal is to discover and develop precious metal deposits. The Company is based in West Perth, Western Australia. The Company has three core projects, two in Western Australia and one in Nevada, USA. The Western Australian projects are still in the exploration stage, and AR continues to focus on developing and delivering high grade, high value resources. The USA project is a share in Nevada gold exploration.

companies.name: Archer Materials
companies.description: Archer Materials, formerly called Archer Exploration, is a public company, trading in the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX:AXE). It started its way developing mineral resources with a vision to develop and integrate advanced materials for use in reliable energy, human health, and quantum technologies for the betterment of society. Archer's business activities span the development of a number of critical minerals and materials, including graphite, cobalt, manganese, copper, and magnesite from exploration through to development and commercialization. In time, Archer Materials grew to become a quantum technology company developing technologies in computing, sensing, and medical diagnostics.

companies.name: China Carbon Graphite Group
companies.description: China Carbon Graphite Group, headquartered in Shanghai (with the main office in the US), manufactures and sells graphite-based products in China.

companies.name: First Graphene
companies.description: First Graphene (FGR), previously First Graphite and in the past was also MRL, aims to become a high quality graphite miner from its Sri Lankan mine prospects, and a graphene producer. The company uses an electrochemical exfoliation to produce high quality graphene from the mined Sri Lankan graphite.

companies.name: Focus Graphite
companies.description: Focus Graphite (previously Focus Metals) is a mid-tier junior graphite company, mine developer and technology company based in Canada. It is the owner of the highest-grade (roughly 16%) technology graphite resource in the world (at Lac Knife in Quebec). The company's goal is to become an industry leader by becoming the lowest-cost producer of technology-grade graphite.

companies.name: Gratomic
companies.description: Gratomic is focused on mining and commercialization of graphite products â specifically graphene-based nano material that can be used for a wide range of mass market elastomer and polymer products, including the global tire market. Gratomic is also developing other industrial applications such as lubricants, special rust, and proof coatings.

companies.name: Hexagon Resources
companies.description: Hexagon Resources is an Australia-based exploration company focusing on the delivery of exceptional high purity and highly crystalline flake graphite for use in new technologies. The primary focus for Hexagon is the development of the McIntosh Flake Graphite Project in the East Kimberley, Western Australia.

companies.name: Leading Edge Materials
companies.description: Leading Edge Materials, formerly Flinders Resources, acquired all of the issued and outstanding shares of Tasman Metals via a plan of arrangement in August 2016. LEM is a Canadian public company (TSX.v:LEM; OTCQB: LEMIF), but its principal assets of are located in Scandinavia. LEMâs core investments are matched to high growth markets, linked to the global shift to low-carbon energy generation and energy storage. LEM's assets and research focus are towards the raw materials for Li-ion batteries (graphite, lithium, high purity aluminium); materials for high thermal efficiency building products (graphite, silica, nepheline); and materials that improve the efficiency of energy generation (dysp

companies.name: Lomiko Metals
companies.description: Lomiko Metals Inc. (TSXV:LMR, OTCQX:LMRMF, FSE:DH8B) is a Canada-based junior miner at the exploration-stage. Lomiko is invested in graphene technologies through Graphene 3D Labs and Graphene ESD .

companies.name: Mason Resources
companies.description: Mason Resources Inc. is a Canadian corporation focused on seeking investment opportunities. Mason is the largest shareholder of Black Swan Graphene Inc. which is focusing on the large-scale production of patented high-performance and low-cost graphene products aimed at several industrial sectors, including polymers and concrete. Mason is also a large shareholder of Nouveau Monde Graphite Inc., an integrated company developing responsible mining and advanced manufacturing operations to supply the global economy with carbon-neutral active anode material to power EV (electric vehicle) and renewable energy storage systems. Mason is a shareholder of Astra Exploration Inc and in NorthX Nickel Corp

companies.name: Matrass C-Graphene
companies.description: Matrass C-Graphene Science-Technology Group is an industrial entity engaging in exploration and development of mineral resources, down-stream processing, fabrication and application of graphene, and R&D of high technology related to the graphite industry.

companies.name: Northern Graphite
companies.description: Northern Graphite Corporation is a Canadian mine development company. It's main asset is the Bissett Creek graphite project located 100km east of North Bay, Ontario. The company was involved with Graphene research back in 2011. Northern Graphite aims to become a vertically integrated mine-to-market company, meeting the growing needs of the North American and European markets. It is focused on becoming a leading global producer of natural battery grade graphite and upgrading it into high-value products critical to the green economy, including anode material for lithium-ion batteries, fuel cells and graphene, as well as advanced industrial technologies. In 2023 Northern said that it acquired a

companies.name: Zentek
companies.description: Zentek Ltd (formerly known as ZEN Graphene Solutions and before that, Zenyatta Ventures ) is a mineral exploration and development company based in Ontario, Canada.

companies.name: Accurion
companies.description: Germany-based Accurion was established in 2009 as a merger between Halcyonics and Nanofilm Technology. The company develops and supplies high-end Imaging Ellipsometry and Active Vibration Isolation equipment.

companies.name: AMO GmbH
companies.description: AMO is a German-based research service provider for material nanofabrication, with competence in nanofabrication, nanoelectronics, nanophotonics and biotechnology. For the graphene industry, AMO offers CVD graphene materials, graphene device (transistors) fabrication, graphene substrates and more.

companies.name: Avansa Technology & Services
companies.description: AVANSA Technology & Services offers analytical testing and consultancy services for industries with emerging nano and micro technology based products. The company also provide wide range of nanotechnology based research services and products.

companies.name: BASF
companies.description: BASF, based in Germany, is one of the world's largest chemical companies - with over 350 production sites worldwide. BASF has been involved with graphene research since 2008 in collaboration with the Max Planck Institute.

companies.name: Cambridge Graphene
companies.description: Cambridge Graphene was established in May 2014 as a spin-off from Cambridge University to commercialize graphene inks based on research work at Cambridge University. Cambridge Graphene in production method is based on a liquid phase exfoliation technology that turns graphite into graphene in a water-based solution. Cambridge Graphene says its technology is unique as it does not start with Graphene Oxide , which results in superior inks with no chemical contamination.

companies.name: Das-nano
companies.description: Spain-based Das-nano produces nanomaterial inspection equipment. For the graphene industry, Das-Nano offers its Onyx system which can be used to quickly obtain information on the uniformity and homogeneity of graphene materials.

companies.name: Future Carbon
companies.description: Future Carbon, based in Germany, develops and manufactures carbon nanomaterials and carbon composites. In April 2013, Future Carbon acquired several graphene and CNT related patents from Bayer , but the company did not update on its graphene R&D work since.

companies.name: Gnanomat
companies.description: Gnanomat, based in Madrid, Spain, developed a proprietary patented liquid-phase procedure to exfoliate graphite to graphene. The single-step process produces high-quality graphene micro platelets. The process uses cheap, biodegradable solvents. The company seeks to find industrial partners to license the technology and scale it to an industrial scale. In February 2017 Gnanomat signed an agreement to co-develop nanomaterials (including graphene) for batteries .

companies.name: GrafTech
companies.description: GrafTech International is a global company with more than 120 years of experience in the carbon and graphite industry.

companies.name: Graphene-Info
companies.description: Graphene-Info, established in 2009, is a knowledge hub focused on the graphene industry. Graphene-Info offers daily graphene industry and science news, with a readership of tens of thousands of professionals a month and over 24,000 subscribers, in addition to a multitude of services to the graphene market based on extensive and up-to-date market intelligence and close ties with industry leaders.

companies.name: HEX 6 Industries
companies.description: HEX 6 Industries Incorporated is a U.S -based company that was founded to develop and market significant advances in green nanotechnology processes and green nanotechnology materials.

companies.name: IBM
companies.description: IBM (NYSE: IBM) is a multinational technology and consulting corporation based in the US. IBM operates several research labs around the world and they are researching graphene related technologies - mostly graphene based transistors and photo detectors.

companies.name: IDTechEx
companies.description: IDTechEx offers independent market research, business intelligence and advice on emerging technologies. IDTechEx offers graphene market reports, and also organizes global graphene events.

companies.name: Intel
companies.description: Intel Corporation, based in the US, is the world's largest semiconductor chip maker (based on revenue). The company supplies chips for PCs, mobile devices and more.

companies.name: JX Advanced Metals
companies.description: Founded in 1905 and headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, JX Advanced Metals is a producer and supplier of non-ferrous metal products, and its activities include resource development, smelting, refining, and recycling. JX Advanced Metals produces high-performance Cu-foils specifically developed for chemical vapor deposition (CVD) graphene growth.

companies.name: Levidian
companies.description: Based in the UK and established in 2012 as Cambridge Nanosystems, Levidian uses patented technology to produce high-grade graphene and hydrogen from waste gas (methane). The company's main product, LOOP, docks into existing infrastructure to strip carbon from gas flow, which could help businesses and national infrastructures to decarbonize.

companies.name: LG
companies.description: LG Corporation, based in South Korea, is a multinational conglomerate corporation that is involved with electronics, displays (LCD, plasma and OLEDs ), telecom, chemicals and more.

companies.name: Metalysis
companies.description: Metalysis was founded in 2001 by the University of Cambridge and located in South Yorkshire, UK. Metalysis owns the global rights to a platform technology capable of producing a wide range of metals and alloys at a lower cost and with a smaller environmental footprint than traditional processes.

companies.name: Nannovative
companies.description: Nannovative is a nanotechnology R&D and engineering company based at the Biotech Campus Delft, in the Netherlands. The company collaborates with startups, universities, research institutes, SMEs, and industrial R&D teams to accelerate the development of graphene, other two-dimensional (2D) materials, and advanced micro- and nanotechnologies.

companies.name: Nanoplexus
companies.description: Nanoplexus develops novel material platforms with 2d materials, such as graphene and MXenes.

companies.name: Nokia
companies.description: Nokia, based in Finland is a large multinational corporation and was once the world's leading mobile phone maker. Nokia Research Center, with its 10 laboratories world-wide, is exploring new technologies mostly for mobility applications.

companies.name: Oxford Advanced Surfaces
companies.description: Oxford Advanced Surfaces Group, based in the UK, designs, develops and manufactures advanced materials for surface modification, adhesion promotion and nano-material applications based on its highly reactive chemical core platform technology called Onto. In March 2014, OASG announced that it is investigating the use of its Onto technology platform to chemically functionalize graphene . In 2020 the company announced a collaboration project with 2-DTech .

companies.name: QuantumWise / Synopsys
companies.description: QuantumWise is a provider of software solutions for development of nanotechnology. The company is working in close collaboration with the Nano-Science Center at the Niels Bohr Institute of Copenhagen University. QuantumWise was acquired by Synopsys in 2017. QuantumWise is offering a system of integrated software modules (called Atomistix Toolkit, or ATK) that can accurately calculate properties associated with electron distribution and transport. It can be used to compute the spin transport in graphene and magnetic nanowires.

companies.name: Samsung
companies.description: Samsung Group, based in South Korea, is a multinational conglomerate company involved with electronics, mobile phones, displays (LCD, Plasma and OLEDs ), materials, insurance, finance, advertising, heavy industry and more.

companies.name: Shandong Yuhuang Chemical
companies.description: Shandong Yuhuang Chemical (Group) is a China-based petrochemical group that produces and markets a range of chemicals, including propylene, isobutene, butadiene, isoprene, Styrene, Toluene, and others. It was founded in 1986 and is located in Heze City, Shandong Province, China.

companies.name: Smithers Apex
companies.description: Smithers Apex, formerly known as IntertechPira, is a global business that provides events, market research, publications and strategic and technical consulting to an expanding list of niche, emerging and high growth industries, including home and personal care; lighting, imaging and displays; plastic electronics and alternative energy.

companies.name: Sony
companies.description: Sony, based in Japan, is one of the leading consumer electronics companies in the world. Years ago, it was known that Sony develops graphene technologies - including a roll to roll production process that can produce graphene sheets up to 100 meters in length .

companies.name: Strategic Energy Resources
companies.description: Strategic Energy Resources (SER) is an Australian based explorer with a diversified portfolio of mineral assets. The company is exploring and developing land with prospective large discoveries in Western Australia, South Australia and Victoria.

companies.name: The Centre for Process Innovation (CPI)
companies.description: The Centre for Process Innovation is a UK-based technology innovation centre. It is a non-profit institute funded by the UK government, the private sector (through contract R&D services) and matched-funding EU projects.

companies.name: Valence Industries
companies.description: Valence Industries is an Australian industrial manufacturing company that produces high grade flake graphite products. In March 2014 Valence launched the Graphene Research Centre in collaboration with the University of Adelaide .

companies.name: Wuxi Feynman Technology
companies.description: China-based Wuxi Feynman Technology (Feynman) focuses on graphene-based materials and systems. The company provides customers services and solutions to customers in the areas of MEMS systems, new graphene materials and compound semiconductor devices, and more. The company also develops 2D deposition equipment.
